title: Decay and structure of heavy flavour
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, talk given by Maria Naeem at SHARP 2026, 4.-7. March 2026, Curia, Portugal
summary: In accordance to the aim of the constituing meeting of the COST action CA24159 ``Structure and Spectroscopy of Hadrons Research Project'' to introduce the different groups to the action, in this talk we give an overview over the subjects dealt with by the working group in Tartu related to hadron physics. We deal with the production and the nonleptonic decays of charmed baryons in the framework of the current algebra approach in terms of tensor invariants and explain how this approach can be used to approach CP violation via long distance effects in rescattering. New physics effects can be even seen in the classical neutron beta decay, but the helicity approach used here is also useful for e.g.\ calculating first order electroweak radiative corrections to the decay of the polarised $W$ boson. Identical particle and mass effects are seen in the Higgs decay into four leptons of the same type. The second main part starts with indications for the intrinsic charm mechanism, explaining the discrepancy between the results of SELEX and LHCb. The solution offered here is valid only if one considers nonlocal field operators. The nonlocal extension of the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, derived directly from QCD and combined with the relativistic Faddeev approach, allows for the description of hadronic states. We conclude by presenting open questions to the action.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses various aspects of hadron physics, focusing on charmed baryon decays, CP violation, and intrinsic charm mechanisms, using advanced theoretical frameworks like current algebra and nonlocal field operators.
AI.motivation: To introduce different research groups to hadron physics topics, fostering collaboration within the COST action CA24159.
AI.method: Utilizes the current algebra approach with tensor invariants and nonlocal extensions of theoretical models derived from QCD, including the relativistic Faddeev approach.
AI.result: Demonstrates how this framework can elucidate CP violation effects, analyze discrepancies in charm production data, and account for unique decay processes in hadron physics.
AI.conclusion: Highlights the need for further exploration of open questions in hadron research and suggests that nonlocal field operator models could reconcile existing discrepancies in experimental results.

title: Phasing out Dark Matter Isocurvature with Thermal Misalignment
summary: Thermal misalignment provides an alternative to the standard misalignment mechanism for the cosmological production of scalar dark matter. In this framework, feeble couplings to particles in the thermal bath generate a finite-temperature potential that drives the scalar towards large field values early in the radiation era, dynamically inducing the misalignment before the onset of scalar oscillations. As a result, the relic abundance is controlled primarily by particle masses and couplings rather than the initial field value. As a light spectator field, the scalar acquires inflationary fluctuations that are uncorrelated with the adiabatic curvature mode, generically sourcing isocurvature perturbations. We show that, unlike standard misalignment, where light scalars are strongly constrained by cosmic microwave background bounds on dark matter isocurvature for high-scale inflation, thermal misalignment can naturally suppress the isocurvature signal. This occurs through a novel late-time phase offset between the background zero mode and the superhorizon perturbations, which reduces the final dark matter density contrast. Thermal misalignment therefore provides a new and generic route to isocurvature-safe scalar dark matter.

AI.tldr: Thermal misalignment offers a novel mechanism for scalar dark matter production, primarily influenced by particle interactions rather than initial conditions.
AI.motivation: To explore a new mechanism for cosmological scalar dark matter production that addresses constraints posed by cosmic microwave background and isocurvature perturbations.
AI.method: Utilizes thermal interactions to create a finite-temperature potential, inducing scalar misalignment early in the radiation era, and analyzing the resulting dynamics and perturbations.
AI.result: Thermal misalignment leads to a reduced isocurvature signal, permitting a wider parameter space for light scalars without conflicting with CMB bounds.
AI.conclusion: This approach provides a generic and viable alternative for producing scalar dark matter that is compatible with observational constraints.

title: Vector Resonances at Muon and Wakefield Colliders
summary: We explore the potential of future high-energy lepton colliders to probe heavy vector resonances. At wakefield colliders, intense beam-beam interactions produce radiation, called beamstrahlung, which redistributes luminosity from the nominal energy across a broad spectrum of lower collision energies. We show that this effect, conventionally viewed as a drawback, dramatically enhances sensitivity to resonances by effectively scanning a wide range of center-of-mass energies. We present projections for a benchmark scenario of a heavy kinetically mixed $Z'$.

AI.tldr: High-energy lepton colliders, particularly wakefield ones, can effectively probe heavy vector resonances by utilizing beamstrahlung effects that broaden collision energy ranges.
AI.motivation: To investigate the capabilities of future high-energy lepton colliders in analyzing heavy vector resonances that may be key to new physics.
AI.method: The study examines the implications of beam-beam interactions at wakefield colliders, focusing on how beamstrahlung can enhance the sensitivity to resonances across various energy levels.
AI.result: The findings indicate that the beamstrahlung effect enhances the collider's ability to scan a wide array of center-of-mass energies, which is beneficial for resonance detection.
AI.conclusion: Utilizing beamstrahlung as a strength rather than a drawback offers a unique approach to exploring heavy vector resonances, exemplified through projections for a heavy kinetically mixed $Z'$.

title: High-Frequency Gravitational Waves from Phase Transitions in Nascent Neutron Stars
summary: Tentative evidence suggests that the cores of massive neutron stars consist of deconfined quark matter. We argue that the formation of such a quark matter core during a galactic supernova could be accompanied by the emission of gravitational waves in the MHz band. These signals constitute a new target for high-frequency gravitational wave detectors, demonstrating that such detectors may offer unique opportunities for testing quantum chromodynamics in an otherwise inaccessible regime.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the potential for gravitational wave emissions during the formation of quark matter cores in massive neutron stars during supernovae, highlighting new opportunities for high-frequency gravitational wave detectors to test theories of quantum chromodynamics.
AI.motivation: To explore the implications of quark matter cores in neutron stars and their potential gravitational wave emissions, which could provide insights into quantum chromodynamics.
AI.method: Examining the theoretical framework for the formation of quark matter cores in supernovae and predicting the associated gravitational wave emissions in the MHz range.
AI.result: Identified gravitational wave signals from quark matter core formation as potential targets for high-frequency detectors, expanding the scope of gravitational wave astronomy.
AI.conclusion: High-frequency gravitational wave detectors may reveal unique characteristics of quark matter and quantum chromodynamics that are otherwise difficult to study.

title: Setting SAIL: Leveraging Scientist-AI-Loops for Rigorous Visualization Tools
comment: 10 pages (+ references), 4 figures. Interactive visualizations available at: https://nicosmo.github.io/lensing_visualization/ and https://nicosmo.github.io/cosmic_web_explorer/
summary: Scientists across all disciplines share a common challenge: the divide between their theoretical knowledge and the specialized skills and time needed to build interactive tools to communicate this expertise. While large language models (LLMs) offer unparalleled acceleration in code generation, they frequently prioritize functional syntax over scientific accuracy, risking visually convincing but scientifically invalid results. This work advocates the Scientist-AI-Loop (SAIL), a framework designed to harness this speed without compromising rigor. By separating domain logic from code syntax, SAIL enables researchers to maintain strict oversight of scientific concepts and constraints while delegating code implementation to AI. We illustrate this approach through two open-source, browser-based astrophysics tools: an interactive gravitational lensing visualization and a large-scale structure formation sandbox, both publicly available. Our methodology condensed development to mere days while maintaining scientific integrity. We specifically address failure modes where AI-generated code neglects phenomenological boundaries or scientific validity. While cautioning that research-grade code requires stringent protocols, we demonstrate through two examples that SAIL provides an effective code generation workflow for outreach, teaching, professional presentations, and early-stage research prototyping. This framework contributes to a foundation for the further development of AI-assisted scientific software.

AI.tldr: The Scientist-AI-Loop (SAIL) framework balances rapid AI code generation with scientific rigor, illustrated via two astrophysics tools, ensuring valid results and facilitating research.
AI.motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and the skills required for creating interactive scientific tools, addressing the limitations of large language models in producing scientifically valid code.
AI.method: SAIL separates domain logic from code syntax, allowing researchers to maintain control over scientific accuracy while leveraging AI for code implementation, as demonstrated through two interactive astrophysics tools.
AI.result: The development of two tools was condensed to days, showcasing the ability of SAIL to uphold scientific integrity despite the rapid code generation.
AI.conclusion: SAIL offers a viable workflow for effective code generation in various scientific contexts, emphasizing the need for stringent protocols for research-grade outputs.

title: Stability of Charge Collection Efficiency and Time Resolution in 4H-SiC PIN Diodes Under X-ray Irradiation
summary: This study evaluates the radiation tolerance of a 4H-SiC PIN detector under X-ray irradiation up to \SI{2}{MGy} (Si) at \SI{160}{keV}. The detector features a fully epitaxial vertical PIN structure with mesa terminations and field plates. Comprehensive pre- and post-irradiation characterization includes I-V/C-V measurements, charge collection efficiency (CCE) and timing resolution tests using $β$-particles ($^{90}$Sr). After \SI{2}{MGy} irradiation, the reverse leakage current remains at an ultralow level of $\sim 10^{-11}$ \si{A/cm^2} at \SI{-300}{V} with negligible degradation. C-V characteristics are basically consistent, with full depletion at \SI{~130}{V}. CCE for $β$-particles decreases by less than 5\%. The detector maintains good timing resolution: \SI{21}{ps} before and \SI{31}{ps} after irradiation, with jitter increasing moderately. These results demonstrate stable performance under extreme X-ray exposure, highlighting the detector's potential for radiation-hard applications in high-energy physics, space missions, and nuclear reactor monitoring.

AI.tldr: This study assesses the radiation tolerance of a 4H-SiC PIN detector subjected to X-ray exposure, finding minimal degradation in performance post-irradiation.
AI.motivation: The goal is to evaluate the robustness of the 4H-SiC PIN detector for applications in high-radiation environments, critical for fields like high-energy physics and space exploration.
AI.method: The detector was characterized using I-V/C-V measurements, charge collection efficiency tests with beta particles, and timing resolution assessment before and after exposure to X-ray irradiation up to 2 MGy at 160 keV.
AI.result: Post-irradiation, the reverse leakage current remained ultralow at approximately 10^-11 A/cm^2, with negligible degradation in C-V characteristics and only a minor reduction in CCE (less than 5%). Timing resolution was slightly affected, with resolutions of 21 ps pre- and 31 ps post-irradiation.
AI.conclusion: The 4H-SiC PIN detector exhibits stable performance even after extreme X-ray exposure, affirming its suitability for radiation-sensitive applications.

title: ADAMOS: Axion Daily Modulation Searches for Dark Matter at 20 GHz
summary: The ADAMOS (Axion Daily Modulation Searches) project aims to explore the nature of dark matter (DM) through a novel axion haloscope experiment. We propose to construct a fixed-frequency cavity resonator operating at 20 GHz at the University of Hamburg, using an innovative "thin-shell" design that preserves a large detection volume at high frequencies. The experiment will be installed in an existing 14 T superconducting magnet and connected to a highly sensitive RF chain with continuous in situ calibration to eliminate temperature-dependent gain drifts, constituting an essential improvement based on lessons learned from previous attempts. ADAMOS will conduct simultaneous searches for three classes of axion signals: (1) conventional cold DM axions, (2) relativistic axions from axion quark nugget annihilations exhibiting daily modulations, and (3) transient enhancements from streaming DM. By targeting this unexplored frequency regime with a robust, calibrated, and versatile setup, ADAMOS will open new discovery channels in a previously unexplored region of the dark sector.

AI.tldr: ADAMOS aims to explore dark matter using a fixed-frequency axion haloscope at 20 GHz, employing an innovative thin-shell design for large detection volume and enhanced sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter, particularly through axion signals, and build on previous experimental learnings.
AI.method: Construct a 20 GHz cavity resonator using a thin-shell design, install it in a 14 T superconducting magnet, and connect it to a sensitive RF chain with continuous calibration.
AI.result: The setup will facilitate simultaneous searches for cold DM axions, relativistic axions from quark nugget annihilations, and transient DM signal enhancements.
AI.conclusion: ADAMOS' novel approach will enable exploration of new discovery channels in the dark sector at unexplored frequency regimes.

title: Fluxes of Generic Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals with a Spinning Secondary
summary: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), comprising a stellar-mass compact object (CO) orbiting a supermassive black hole (BH), are key targets for future space-based gravitational-wave (GW) observatories. Incorporating the spin of the secondary body into waveform models not only enhances measurement precision but also offers insight into the spin distribution of stellar-mass objects. In this work, we construct the flux and waveform for an EMRI with a spinning secondary in a Kerr background under the linear-spin approximation. Using the radiative prescription (half-retarded minus half-advanced field), we derive orbit-averaged evolution equations for the fundamental constants of motion, including the energy, angular momentum, Carter-like constant, and the parallel spin component. This framework provides a tractable route to generating waveforms that incorporate the secondary spin, with the potential for further simplification in future work.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a framework for calculating gravitational waveforms from extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) that consider the spin of a stellar-mass compact object orbiting a supermassive black hole.
AI.motivation: To improve measurement precision of gravitational waves and understand the spin distribution of stellar-mass objects.
AI.method: The flux and waveform are constructed in a Kerr background under linear-spin approximation using a radiative prescription to derive orbit-averaged evolution equations for constants of motion.
AI.result: A tractable framework is established for generating waveforms that include the secondary spin component, with prospects for further simplification.
AI.conclusion: This framework enhances the capability of modeling EMRIs, paving the way for improved insights into gravitational wave observables.

title: Asymptotic Expansions for Neural Network Approximations of Quantum Channels
summary: This paper establishes the Quantum Voronovskaya--Damasclin (QVD) Theorem, providing a complete asymptotic characterization of Quantum Neural Network Operators in the approximation of arbitrary quantum channels. The result extends the classical Voronovskaya theorem from scalar approximation to the non-commutative operator framework of quantum information theory. We introduce rigorous quantum analogues of Sobolev and Hölder spaces defined through Fréchet differentiability in the Liouville representation and measured using the completely bounded (diamond) norm. Within this framework, we derive an explicit asymptotic expansion of the approximation error and identify the fundamental mechanisms governing convergence. The expansion separates integer-order differential contributions, fractional corrections associated with limited regularity, and intrinsically non-commutative effects arising from operator algebra structure. We also establish a sharp remainder estimate with explicit dependence on the regularity of the channel and the dimension of the underlying Hilbert space. Several applications demonstrate the scope of the theory. These include a quantum central limit theorem describing the fluctuation regime of quantum neural network operators, an optimal interpolation method based on operator geometric means, and a convergence acceleration procedure inspired by Richardson extrapolation. The results provide a rigorous mathematical foundation for the asymptotic analysis of quantum neural network models and establish a direct connection between classical approximation theory, operator algebras, and quantum information science, with implications for quantum algorithms and quantum machine learning.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the Quantum Voronovskaya--Damasclin Theorem, characterizing Quantum Neural Network Operators' asymptotic behavior in approximating quantum channels.
AI.motivation: To extend the classical Voronovskaya theorem to the realm of quantum information, specifically for non-commutative operators.
AI.method: Rigorous quantum analogues of Sobolev and Hölder spaces are developed using Fréchet differentiability and the completely bounded norm, leading to an asymptotic expansion of the approximation error.
AI.result: An explicit expansion of the approximation error is derived, detailing contributions from integer-order, fractional, and non-commutative effects, along with a sharp remainder estimate.
AI.conclusion: The findings enhance understanding of quantum neural networks and their approximation capabilities, linking classical theory with quantum information science, and offering practical implications for quantum algorithms and machine learning.

title: Two-Component Dark Matter in the Type-I 2HDM
summary: We investigate a two-component dark matter scenario in the type-I two-Higgs-doublet model. The dark sector contains a real scalar $s$ and a Dirac fermion $χ$, whose stability is ensured by a $Z_4$ symmetry together with kinematic conditions. The scalar interacts with the visible sector through Higgs-portal couplings, while the fermion interacts with the scalar via Yukawa interactions. In this framework, we analyze the thermal freeze-out production of both candidates, accounting for annihilation, conversion, and semi-annihilation processes. A comprehensive scan over the multidimensional parameter space is performed in terms of physical masses, mixing angles, and portal couplings, imposing theoretical requirements such as perturbativity and vacuum stability. We confront the model with current experimental constraints, including the observed relic abundance, invisible Higgs decays, direct detection limits on spin-independent scattering cross sections, and electroweak precision observables. We find that viable regions of parameter space can satisfy all dark matter constraints, but collider bounds strongly constrain the scalar sector, narrowing the allowed regions and creating tension with those favored by dark matter phenomenology, particularly in the sub-TeV mass regime.

AI.tldr: This study explores a multi-component dark matter model within the type-I two-Higgs-doublet framework, analyzing thermal production processes and confronting the model with experimental constraints.
AI.motivation: To understand the feasibility and constraints of a two-component dark matter scenario in the context of the type-I two-Higgs-doublet model.
AI.method: The authors examine dark matter candidates (a real scalar and a Dirac fermion) considering their production through thermal freeze-out, and analyze the parameter space including interactions through scalar and Yukawa couplings, imposing theoretical constraints.
AI.result: The scan over the parameter space identifies viable regions that meet dark matter requirements, although collider constraints significantly limit the scalar sector and lead to tension in the sub-TeV mass range.
AI.conclusion: While certain parameter choices align with dark matter phenomenology, stringent collider limits restrict the allowed configurations, indicating a conflict between dark matter viability and collider observables.

title: ALABI: Active Learning for Accelerated Bayesian Inference
summary: We present Active Learning for Accelerated Bayesian Inference (\texttt{alabi}): an open-source Python package for performing Bayesian inference with computationally expensive models. Given a forward model and observational data to construct a likelihood and priors, \texttt{alabi}\ uses a Gaussian Process (GP) surrogate model trained to predict posterior probability as a function of input parameters, and employs active learning to iteratively improve GP predictive performance in high-likelihood regions where the GP is most uncertain. \texttt{alabi}\ provides a uniform interface for using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) with different packages, including the affine-invariant sampler \texttt{emcee}, and nested samplers \texttt{dynesty}, \texttt{multinest}, and \texttt{ultranest}. This approach facilitates accurate estimation of the desired posterior distribution, while reducing the number of computationally expensive model evaluations required by factors of thousands. We demonstrate the performance of \texttt{alabi}\ on a variety of test cases, including where inference is challenging due to complex posterior structure or high dimensionality. We show that \texttt{alabi}\ offers a substantial improvement for likelihood functions with evaluation times $\gtrsim 1$\,s, speeding up MCMC computations by a factor of $10-1000\times$ when tested on problems with up to 64 dimensions.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces 	exttt{alabi}, an open-source Python package that accelerates Bayesian inference via active learning and Gaussian Process surrogates, significantly reducing computation time for high-dimensional problems.
AI.motivation: To address the computational challenges in Bayesian inference with expensive models, particularly when evaluating likelihood functions takes substantial time.
AI.method: exttt{alabi} utilizes a Gaussian Process surrogate model trained to predict posterior probabilities and employs active learning to enhance predictive performance in regions of high likelihood uncertainty. It integrates with various MCMC packages for efficient posterior distribution estimation.
AI.result: The implementation of 	exttt{alabi} demonstrates significant improvements, achieving speedups of 10-1000 times in MCMC computations for high-dimensional inference problems, especially those with likelihood evaluations exceeding 1 second.
AI.conclusion: exttt{alabi} provides a robust and efficient framework for Bayesian inference, effectively minimizing the number of expensive model evaluations necessary for accurate posterior estimation.

title: Spatial resolution improvement of PICOSEC Micromegas precise timing detectors
summary: The combination of a Cherenkov radiator with a semi-transparent photocathode and a Micromegas based amplification stage allows PICOSEC Micromegas detectors to achieve a time resolution of better than 15ps. While tileable prototypes with 10x10 channels feature 1x1 cm^2 readout pads, finer readout granularity can be used to improve the spatial resolution. We report on the study of high readout granularity PICOSEC Micromegas prototypes which achieve around 0.5mm spatial resolution with 3.5mm large pads. No significant improvement was found when readout pad size was further reduced to 2.2mm. The timing resolution of the leading pad was found to be slightly degraded but remained better than 20ps for a medium granularity prototype. The achieved spatial resolution can enable PICOSEC Micromegas to be used as precise timing and moderate resolution tracking detector simultaneously.

AI.tldr: PICOSEC Micromegas detectors combine a Cherenkov radiator with a photocathode and achieve a time resolution under 15ps and spatial resolution of around 0.5mm.
AI.motivation: To enhance the performance of particle detectors in terms of timing and spatial resolution.
AI.method: Integrate a Cherenkov radiator, a semi-transparent photocathode, and a Micromegas amplification stage in high readout granularity prototypes.
AI.result: Prototypes achieved approximately 0.5mm spatial resolution with medium granularity, and timing resolution remained better than 20ps.
AI.conclusion: The design allows for precise timing and moderate resolution tracking, demonstrating the potential for use in advanced detection systems.

title: A search for lepton-flavour violating $τ\to 3μ$ decays with the ATLAS detector
comment: 37 pages in total, author list starting page 20, 4 figures, 3 tables, submitted to Phy. Lett. B. All figures including auxiliary figures are available a https://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/PHYSICS/PAPERS/BPHY-2018-05
summary: A search for charged lepton flavour violation in $τ\to 3μ$ decays is performed in $pp$ collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV using ATLAS data collected between 2016 and 2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 137 $\text{fb}^{-1}$. The search focuses on the electroweak $W \to τν$ production channel. Data are collected using two-muon and three-muon triggers and a multivariate analysis is used to separate the signal from the background. An unbinned likelihood fit is then performed to the resulting three-muon invariant mass spectrum and the data are found to be compatible with the background-only hypothesis. The observed (expected) limit on the branching ratio $B(τ\to3μ)$ is found to be $8.7\times 10^{-8}$ ($7.5\times 10^{-8}$) at $90\%$ CL.

AI.tldr: A search for the decay process $τ\to 3μ$ in 13 TeV $pp$ collisions found no evidence of charged lepton flavour violation, setting a limit on the branching ratio.
AI.motivation: To investigate potential charged lepton flavour violation in the decay process $τ\to 3μ$, which could provide insights into physics beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: Utilized ATLAS data from 13 TeV $pp$ collisions with an integrated luminosity of 137 $	ext{fb}^{-1}$. Employed two-muon and three-muon triggers, followed by a multivariate analysis to distinguish signal from background, and performed an unbinned likelihood fit on the three-muon invariant mass spectrum.
AI.result: Data analysis showed compatibility with the background-only hypothesis. The observed limit on the branching ratio was $8.7\times 10^{-8}$, while the expected limit was $7.5\times 10^{-8}$ at 90% CL.
AI.conclusion: The results provide no evidence for lepton flavour violation in the $τ\to 3μ$ decay and establish stringent upper limits on the decay's branching ratio.

title: Discovery of Bimodal Drift Rate Structure in FRB 20240114A: Evidence for Dual Emission Regions
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We report the discovery of bimodal structure in the drift rate distribution of upward-drifting burst clusters from the hyperactive repeating fast radio burst FRB 20240114A. Using unsupervised machine learning (UMAP dimensionality reduction combined with HDBSCAN density-based clustering) applied to 233 upward-drifting burst clusters from the FAST telescope dataset, we identify a distinct subpopulation of 45 burst clusters (Cluster C1) with mean drift rates 2.5x higher than typical upward-drifting burst clusters (245.6 vs 98.1 MHz/ms). Gaussian mixture modeling reveals strong evidence for bimodality (delta-BIC = 296.6), with clearly separated modes (Ashman's D = 2.70 > 2) and a statistically significant gap in the distribution (11.3 sigma). Crucially, we demonstrate that this bimodality persists when restricting the analysis to single-component (U1) burst clusters only (delta-BIC = 19.9, Ashman's D = 2.71), confirming that the result is not an artifact of combining single- and multi-component burst clusters with different drift rate definitions. The extreme-drift subpopulation also exhibits systematically lower peak frequencies (-7%), shorter durations (-29%), and distinct clustering in multi-dimensional feature space. These findings are suggestive of two spatially separated emission regions in the magnetosphere, each producing upward-drifting burst clusters with distinct physical characteristics, although confirmation requires observations from additional epochs and sources.

AI.tldr: Discovery of bimodal structure in drift rate distribution of burst clusters from FRB 20240114A, indicating two distinct emission regions.
AI.motivation: To explore the drift rate characteristics of upward-drifting burst clusters and understand their underlying mechanisms.
AI.method: Applied UMAP and HDBSCAN on 233 burst clusters, revealing a distinct subpopulation with higher drift rates, supported by Gaussian mixture modeling for bimodality.
AI.result: Identified a bimodal distribution with a distinct subpopulation (C1) and confirmed the findings through restriction to single-component clusters, showing lower frequencies and shorter durations.
AI.conclusion: Findings indicate two spatially separated emission regions in the magnetosphere producing distinct burst clusters, calling for further observations to confirm.

title: Advanced Quantum Annealing for the Bi-Objective Traveling Thief Problem: An $\varepsilon$-Constraint-based Approach
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, and 3 tables. Accepted by IEEE Transactions on Quantum Engineering
summary: This paper addresses the Bi-Objective Traveling Thief Problem (BI-TTP), a challenging multi-objective optimization problem that requires the simultaneous optimization of travel cost and item profit. Conventional methods for the BI-TTP often face severe scalability issues due to the complex interdependence between routing and packing decisions, as well as the inherent complexity and large problem size. These difficulties render classical computing approaches increasingly inapplicable. To tackle this, we propose an advanced hybrid approach that combines quantum annealing (QA) with the $\varepsilon$-constraint method. Specifically, we reformulate the bi-objective problem into a single-objective formulation by restricting the second objective through adjustable $\varepsilon$-levels, determined within established upper and lower bounds. The resulting subproblem involves a sum of fractional terms, which is reformulated with auxiliary variables into an equivalent form. Subsequently, the equivalent formulation is transformed into a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model, enabling direct solution via a quantum annealing (QA) solver. The solutions obtained from the quantum annealer are subsequently refined using a tailored heuristic procedure to further enhance overall performance. By leveraging the flexibility in selecting $\varepsilon$ parameters, our approach effectively captures a broad Pareto front, enhancing solution diversity. Experimental results on benchmark instances demonstrate that the proposed method effectively balances two objectives and outperforms baseline approaches in time efficiency.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an advanced hybrid approach for solving the Bi-Objective Traveling Thief Problem by combining quantum annealing and the epsilon-constraint method.
AI.motivation: The BI-TTP presents significant scalability issues due to complex interdependencies in routing and packing decisions, making classical approaches less effective.
AI.method: The method reformulates the bi-objective problem into a single-objective format using epsilon-level restrictions, converts it into a QUBO model for quantum annealing, and applies a heuristic for solution refinement.
AI.result: The proposed hybrid method captures a broad Pareto front and outperforms traditional methods in balancing travel cost and item profit while improving time efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Experimental results confirm the hybrid approach's effectiveness, demonstrating enhanced solution diversity and performance over baseline methods.

title: Axions at the meV Crossroads: Theory, Cosmology, Astrophysics, and Experiments
summary: The meV mass range has emerged as a focal point in axion physics, where advances in theory, cosmology, astrophysics, and experimental techniques converge. Axions in this mass range are theoretically well motivated, can arise in ultraviolet-complete models, and can have significant cosmological impacts as dark matter or dark radiation. In parallel, their efficient production in stellar and supernova environments provides powerful astrophysical probes. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of meV axions across these domains, highlighting both established results and open questions. We discuss the theoretical underpinnings of meV axions, their cosmological and astrophysical signatures, and the diverse experimental strategies -- ranging from helioscopes and haloscopes to quasiparticle systems and large-volume Cherenkov detectors -- that aim to explore this regime. The convergence of these approaches emphasizes the pivotal role of the meV mass range for axion discovery in the coming years, identifying meV axions as a key probe for testing beyond-Standard-Model physics. This review document is the direct outcome of the discussions at the dedicated workshop "The meV Mass Axion Frontier: Challenges and Opportunities", held at Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati (IT) on 27--28 October 2025, and organized by the EU funded COST Action "Cosmic WISPers in the Dark Universe: Theory, astrophysics, and experiments" (CA21106, https://www.cost.eu/actions/CA21106). Its aim is to provide an overview of current efforts in meV axion research, their motivations, and the research goals that animate the community involved in this search.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the significance of meV axions in physics, discussing theoretical and experimental aspects, their role as dark matter or dark radiation, and the motivations behind current research efforts.
AI.motivation: The meV mass range is critical for axion physics due to its potential links with dark matter and beyond-Standard-Model physics, necessitating a comprehensive overview amidst ongoing research.
AI.method: The paper synthesizes theoretical insights, cosmological and astrophysical implications, and experimental approaches, including helioscopes, haloscopes, and large-volume detectors.
AI.result: The review highlights both established knowledge and remaining uncertainties regarding meV axions, emphasizing their importance as probes of new physics.
AI.conclusion: The document aims to foster collaboration and guide future research on meV axions, showcasing their central role in understanding fundamental physics.

title: cosmo-numba: B-modes and COSEBIs computations accelerated by Numba
summary: Weak gravitational lensing is a widely used probe in cosmological analysis. It allows astrophysists to understand the content and evolution of the Universe. We are entering an era where we are not limited by the data volume but by systematic uncertainties. It is in this context that we present here a simple python-based software package to help in the computation of E-/B-mode decomposition, which can be use for systematic checks or science analysis. As we demonstrate, our implementation has both the high precision and speed required to perform this kind of analysis while avoiding a scenario wherein either numerical precision or computational time is a significant limiting factor.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a Python software package for E-/B-mode decomposition in weak gravitational lensing analyses, addressing systematic uncertainties.
AI.motivation: The need to tackle systematic uncertainties in weak gravitational lensing data analysis, as we move beyond data volume limitations.
AI.method: Development of a Python-based software for E-/B-mode decomposition that emphasizes precision and speed.
AI.result: The software demonstrates high precision and efficiency in analysis, minimizing limitations due to numerical precision and computational time.
AI.conclusion: The presented software package is a valuable tool for researchers in cosmology to ensure reliable analysis amid systematic uncertainties.

title: A Minimal-Component 100 MHz Full-Duplex Digital Link Over a Single Coaxial Cable for Laboratory Instrumentation
comment: 7 pages, 10 figures. This preprint has been submitted to Review of Scientific Instruments published by the American Institute of Physics
summary:
We present a minimal-component bidirectional digital interconnect that enables simultaneous transmission and reception of baseband logic signals over a single coaxial cable. The circuit consists of a passive resistive hybrid providing matched line termination and directional separation, a single CMOS logic gate as driver, and a commercial LVDS receiver used as a differential comparator. No active echo cancellation, calibration, or transformer coupling is required.
  An analytical treatment of the hybrid network is used to determine the system parameter that maximizes the received signal amplitude. SPICE simulations predict deterministic timing errors caused by incomplete separation of transmitted and received signals. Experimental measurements confirm the predicted deterministic jitter and show good agreement with the simulation results.
  For typical laboratory coaxial cables up to 6 m, the measured peak-to-peak edge timing error remains below 1 ns. A bidirectional transmission experiment with randomized data at 250 MBaud demonstrates a clearly open eye diagram and confirms reliable full-duplex operation. Due to its simplicity and compatibility with existing coaxial infrastructure, the proposed approach may be useful in laboratory and detector environments where cable routing or feedthrough density is constrained.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a minimal-component bidirectional digital interconnect for simultaneous signal transmission and reception via a single coaxial cable, emphasizing simplicity and performance without active components.
AI.motivation: The aim is to create a straightforward solution for bidirectional communication that is compatible with existing coaxial cable infrastructure, addressing constraints in laboratory settings
AI.method: The approach utilizes a passive resistive hybrid for signal separation, a CMOS logic gate as a driver, and a commercial LVDS receiver for signal comparison, avoiding the need for active components.
AI.result: The experimental setup showed that the timing error for signals transmitted over typical laboratory coaxial cables remains below 1 ns, with successful full-duplex operation demonstrated at 250 MBaud.
AI.conclusion: The proposed interconnect design offers a practical solution for reliable communication in constrained environments, highlighting its potential utility in various laboratory and detector applications.

title: Reconstruction of overlapping electromagnetic showers in calorimeters using Transformers
summary: Accurate clustering of electromagnetic energy deposits is essential for reconstructing photons and electrons in modern hadron collider experiments, where boosted topologies and pileup cause overlapping showers and ambiguous energy assignment. We present deep learning-based clustering approaches that reconstruct particle energy and position directly from calorimeter readout. The study includes a two-step strategy in which candidate seed windows are identified and then jointly processed via distance-weighted message passing or attention mechanism and a single-step graph transformer, ClusTEX, which performs candidate selection and reconstruction in one inference stage. ClusTEX uses a novel positional encoding scheme that separates local coordinates within the graph from global detector coordinates, enabling efficient, geometry-aware inference. Models are trained on GEANT4 simulations of a simplified (toy) and an ECAL-inspired topology with an explicit $η-φ$ dependence. Performance is evaluated using efficiency, energy and position resolutions and splitting rate - reconstruction of two objects for a single photon. In the toy calorimeter, attention-based interactions improve the reconstruction of overlapping showers relative to both the standard algorithm and distance-driven message passing, while maintaining performance on isolated photons and reducing splitting without multi-pass inference. For boosted $π^0\toγγ$, the attention-based model retains di-photon mass reconstruction capability, where the standard algorithm becomes inefficient. In the ECAL-inspired topology, ClusTEX provides the best overall performance, yielding improved energy resolution and reduced splitting compared to two-step approaches and the standard algorithm. It also remains robust under localized detector failures, showing improved stability and partial recovery of energy in non-responsive channels.

AI.tldr: Deep learning approaches for clustering electromagnetic energy deposits improve photon/electron reconstruction by enhancing overlapping showers and efficiency.
AI.motivation: Accurate clustering is critical due to challenges in modern collider experiments such as overlapping energy deposits and pileup effects.
AI.method: Introduces a two-step strategy with distance-weighted message passing and attention mechanisms, alongside a single-step graph transformer called ClusTEX, which uses a novel positional encoding scheme.
AI.result: ClusTEX outperforms standard algorithms and two-step methods in energy resolution, splitting rate, and robustness against detector failures, especially for overlapping showers and di-photon mass identification.
AI.conclusion: Deep learning consistently enhances reconstruction capabilities in complex particle interactions, demonstrating superior performance and stability under various conditions.

title: Probing Kerr black hole in a uniform Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field through astrophysical quasi-periodic oscillations
summary: In this study, the behavior of high-frequency quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) is investigated around a Kerr black hole immersed in a uniform Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field. The motion of the test particle is analyzed by determining the geodesic equations and evaluating the corresponding orbital, radial, and vertical epicyclic frequencies. These fundamental frequencies are used to construct the theoretical framework of QPO models based on parametric and forced resonance mechanisms. Observational data obtained from several black hole X-ray binaries (GRO J1655-40, XTE J1550-564, XTE J1859+226, GRS 1915+105, H1743-322, M82~X-1, and Sgr~A$^{*}$) are used to constrain the black hole parameters through Bayesian inference and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analyses. For the X-ray binaries GRO J1655-40, GRS 1915+105, H1743-322, and M82~X-1, nonzero values of the dimensionless parameter $b=Bm$ are obtained at the $68\%$ confidence level within the framework of the parametric resonance model, while only upper bounds at the $90\%$ confidence level are obtained for the remaining sources. In contrast, in the case of the forced resonance model, only an upper bound at the $90\%$ confidence interval is obtained for the magnetic field parameter for all considered X-ray binary sources. The analysis indicates that the value of the magnetic field parameter is small but not negligible, producing minor modifications to particle dynamics and epicyclic frequencies. The influence of the magnetic field is further examined through the properties of the innermost stable circular orbit and the radiative properties of the thin accretion disk, including the energy flux and temperature profiles, within the allowed parameter range inferred from the MCMC analysis.

AI.tldr: This study investigates high-frequency quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) around a Kerr black hole in a magnetic field, analyzing test particle motion and observational data from X-ray binaries to infer black hole parameters.
AI.motivation: To understand the influence of magnetic fields on the dynamics of high-frequency QPOs in the vicinity of Kerr black holes, and to leverage observational data for parameter estimation.
AI.method: Geodesic equations are determined to analyze particle motion, while QPO models based on parametric and forced resonance mechanisms are constructed using observational data analyzed via Bayesian inference and MCMC techniques.
AI.result: Nonzero values for the dimensionless parameter related to the magnetic field were found for some black hole binaries at 68% confidence, while upper bounds were noted for others. The forced resonance model yielded only upper bounds across all sources.
AI.conclusion: The magnetic field parameter is small yet significant, influencing particle dynamics and features of the accretion disk, affirming the need for further exploration of magnetic effects on QPO behavior.

title: Some Studies On Exact Solutions Of Models In Noncommutative Spaces
comment: Ph. D Thesis (2024), Advisor : Prof. Sunandan Gangopadhyay, Collaborator : Dr. Shreemoyee Ganguly
summary: The central theme of my thesis is to explore various simple prototype models that are exactly solvable in the framework of time dependent noncommutative spaces. By adopting the methodology provided by the Lewis Riesenfeld theory, we developed a procedure for obtaining a class of exact solutions for such model systems. We analyzed these solutions by deriving the energy expectation values analytically and representing those energy dynamics graphically. We also examined the explicit existence of a non-zero Berry geometric phase in the noncommutative framework and analyzed the role of noncommutativity in generating a non-trivial Berry phase when the model Hamiltonian and the noncommutative parameters are periodic in time. Overall, my thesis contributes to a deeper understanding of quantum theory in time dependent noncommutative backgrounds and indicates a strong possibility for developing a consistent quantum theory within such frameworks.

AI.tldr: This thesis investigates solvable models in time dependent noncommutative spaces, presenting exact solutions and examining their energy dynamics and Berry phases.
AI.motivation: To deepen the understanding of quantum theory in noncommutative spaces and explore solvable models for theoretical development.
AI.method: Application of Lewis Riesenfeld theory to develop exact solutions, analyze energy expectation values analytically, and study the Berry geometric phase.
AI.result: Derived exact solutions and explored energy dynamics, revealing the presence of a non-zero Berry phase due to noncommutativity.
AI.conclusion: The research indicates a strong potential for a consistent quantum theory in time dependent noncommutative frameworks.

title: Stellar Bounds on a Model with Photon-Photino Oscillation
summary: In this paper, we pursue an investigation of the consequences of a mixing between supersymmetric partners - the photon and photino - analogous to the so-called Primakoff effect, but induced by a Lorentz-symmetry violating (LSV) fermionic-condensate background. In our framework, the LSV parameters are introduced as members of a non-dynamical superfield. As a consequence, we show that naturally there appears a mixing term between the gauge boson and the gaugino, which can be readily seen in the superspace/superfield approach. We inspect the kinetic photon-photino mixing matrix in the scenario of stellar physics which we apply our results to. Bounds on the strength of the fermionic LSV background are can be set by invoking the energy loss argument and the solar data we adopt.

AI.tldr: This paper examines how mixing between supersymmetric partners, specifically the photon and photino, occurs due to a Lorentz-symmetry violating (LSV) background, extending the Primakoff effect. It introduces LSV parameters via a non-dynamical superfield, leading to a photon-photino mixing term, and applies its findings to constraints in stellar physics using solar energy loss data.
AI.motivation: To explore new physics implications of mixing between supersymmetric partners in the context of Lorentz symmetry violation.
AI.method: Introduces LSV parameters as a non-dynamical superfield and analyzes the resulting photon-photino mixing in a superspace framework.
AI.result: Identifies a mixing term between gauge bosons and gauginos, allowing for the evaluation of physical effects in stellar scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Provides constraints on the strength of fermionic LSV backgrounds using solar energy loss data.

title: One-week optical observations of pulsed emission from the Crab pulsar with IMONY on the 3.8 m Seimei telescope
summary: We report our optical observations of the Crab pulsar using the Imager of MPPC-based Optical photoN counter from Yamagata (IMONY), a high-time-resolution photon-counting imager with 100 ns timing resolution, mounted on the 3.8 m Seimei telescope in Japan (f/D~6). The detector format was upgraded from a $4\times4$ to an $8\times8$ GAPD array with larger pixels ($100$ to $200~{μm}$), resulting in a 14".5 field of view on the Seimei telescope. We conducted nightly optical observations for one week, including two nights of simultaneous optical and radio observations with the 64 m Usuda radio telescope. Thanks to the large diameter of the Seimei telescope and the high time resolution of IMONY, we successfully detected optical Single Pulses (SPs) emitted in each rotation. Moreover, we found an optical peak timing drift of $30\pm7.9~\mathrm{μs}$ over three days, with a significance of $3.9σ$. The corresponding emission region size is 9.1 km, which is equivalent to 0.006 times the light cylinder radius of the Crab pulsar. We ruled out the possibility of a pulsar glitch and suggested that the optical pulsed emission region of the Crab pulsar may fluctuate due to the spatial drift and variations in the magnetospheric caustics.

AI.tldr: This study presents optical observations of the Crab pulsar using an upgraded photon-counting imager, achieving significant findings regarding single-pulse emissions and optical peak timing drifts.
AI.motivation: To observe optical emissions from the Crab pulsar and understand the nature of its optical pulsed emission region.
AI.method: Utilized an upgraded IMONY detector on the 3.8 m Seimei telescope, conducting nightly optical observations and simultaneous radio observations for data collection.
AI.result: Detected optical Single Pulses with a timing drift of $30\pm7.9~\mathrm{μs}$ over three days, with a significance of $3.9σ$ and a corresponding emission region size of 9.1 km.
AI.conclusion: Optical emissions may fluctuate due to magnetospheric changes, ruled out pulsar glitches as the cause of timing drifts.

title: A Sub-electron-noise Skipper-CCD Readout ASIC with Improved Channel-to-channel Isolation and an Integrated Cryogenic Voltage Reference
comment: Submitted to IEEE Instrumentation and Measurements. 8 pages, 10 figures, previous publication: arXiv:2304.13088
summary: The MIDNA application specific integrated circuits (ASICs) are a series of skipper-CCD readout chips fabricated in a 65 nm low-power CMOS process that implement a correlated double sampling signal processing chain based on dual-slope integrators. They are capable of working from room to cryogenic temperatures, down to 84 K. The present iteration of the ASIC has been fabricated including several design updates and the addition of an on-chip voltage reference, resulting in improved performance. This work presents the main vulnerabilities solved, the changes carried out, and the resulting performance benefits. Measurements with a skipper-CCD and the ASIC at 140 K showed that the single-electron resolution can be reached by averaging the measured charge in the analog domain using the analog pile-up technique with a readout noise as low as 0.11 erms of equivalent charge for 1200 samples. The channel-to-channel crosstalk was also characterized showing values better than -62 dB.

AI.tldr: MIDNA ASICs enhance skipper-CCD readout with dual-slope integrators, achieving single-electron resolution at low temperatures.
AI.motivation: To improve the performance of skipper-CCD readouts in various temperature ranges, particularly at cryogenic levels, by addressing vulnerabilities and optimizing design.
AI.method: Utilized a 65 nm low-power CMOS process for ASICs with updates including an on-chip voltage reference and implemented correlated double sampling via dual-slope integrators.
AI.result: Achieved single-electron resolution through analog charge averaging at 140 K with readout noise of 0.11 erms for 1200 samples, and demonstrated channel-to-channel crosstalk better than -62 dB.
AI.conclusion: The updated MIDNA ASICs significantly enhance performance for skipper-CCD applications, especially in low-temperature environments.

title: Observation of $D_s^+ \to a_0(980)^+f_0(500)$ in the Amplitude Analysis of $D_s^+ \to π^+ π^0 π^0 η$
summary: We report the first observation of the decay $D_s^+ \to π^+π^0π^0η$ in a data set corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 7.33 fb$^{-1}$, collected in $e^+e^-$ collisions by the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies between 4.128 and 4.226 GeV. An unexpectedly large branching fraction $\mathcal{B}( D_s^+ \to a_0(980)^+ f_0(500), a_0(980)^+ \to π^+η, f_0(500)\to π^0π^0) = (0.98 \pm 0.16_{\rm{stat.}} \pm 0.22_{\rm{syst.}})\%$ is measured with a significance exceeding $10σ$, offering new constraints on the internal structure of light scalar mesons. The dominant intermediate process is $D_s^+ \to a_1(1260)^+η, a_1(1260)^+\to ρ(770)^+π^0$ with a branching fraction of $(1.77 \pm 0.21_{\rm stat.} \pm 0.12_{\rm syst.})\%$. The isospin symmetry has been validated to the decays of $a_1(1260)^+\to ρ(770)^0π^+$ and $a_1(1260)^+\to ρ(770)^+π^0$. Moreover, the measured $\mathcal{B}(D_s^+\to π^+π^0π^0η|_{\rm{non}-η^\prime})=(2.97 \pm 0.23_{\rm stat.} \pm 0.14_{\rm sys.})$ reduces the undetected $D_s^+ \to ηX$ decay branching fractions to (0.1 $\pm$ 3.1)\%.

AI.tldr: The first observation of the decay $D_s^+ \to π^+π^0π^0η$ is reported, with a significant branching fraction, offering insights into light scalar mesons' structure and validating isospin symmetry in related decays.
AI.motivation: To explore the decay mechanisms and branching fractions of the $D_s^+$ meson, focusing particularly on new decay channels and their significance in understanding light scalar mesons.
AI.method: Data collected from $e^+e^-$ collisions by the BESIII detector at varying energies, with subsequent analysis to measure the branching fractions of various decay processes.
AI.result: A significant branching fraction for $D_s^+ \to a_0(980)^+ f_0(500)$ is observed, alongside the dominant process $D_s^+ \to a_1(1260)^+η$, confirming isospin symmetry and leading to reduced estimates of other branching fractions.
AI.conclusion: The findings enhance the understanding of light scalar mesons and validate isospin symmetry, while the newly measured branching fractions highlight previously unrecognized decay paths.

title: Spectral Hardness as the Primary Discriminator: Unveiling the Collapsar--Merger Boundary with a Gold-Standard Gamma-Ray Burst Sample
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures and 2 tables; accepted by APJ Letters
summary: In this Letter, we establish a robust, physically motivated classification method using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) trained on a "gold-standard" sample of 24 GRBs with spectroscopically confirmed progenitors (associated SNe or KNe). By isolating the prompt main spike to excise contamination from extended emission, we derive a quantitative classification index, I_SVM = 5.01 log_10 E_p,i - 1.25 log_10 E_iso - 0.34 log_10 T_90,z - 12.90 (units: keV, 10^52 erg, s). Events with I_SVM > 0 are classified as mergers. Analysis of the standardized classification weights reveals that the discriminative power of E_p,i is approximately 5 times that of T_90,z, while E_iso contributes a weight comparable to E_p,i. This quantitatively demonstrates that spectral hardness and energetics, rather than duration, are the primary physical signatures distinguishing mergers from collapsars. The derived boundary implies a stringent hardness ceiling for collapsars, while mergers are identified as outliers with excessive hardness relative to their energy budget. The classifier successfully identifies the nature of historic test cases, including the ultra-long GRB 111209A (collapsar) and the short GRB 050709 (merger), independent of instrumental eras. This tool paves the way for cleaning archival and future high-redshift GRB samples for precision cosmology.

AI.tldr: This study presents a classification method using SVM to distinguish between GRB progenitors. A classification index is derived that emphasizes spectral hardness and energetics.
AI.motivation: To create a reliable classification method for Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) and understand the physical differences between their progenitors, specifically mergers and collapsars.
AI.method: A Support Vector Machine is trained on a sample of 24 GRBs with confirmed progenitors. The analysis isolates the prompt spike to minimize contamination, leading to a quantitative classification index from physical parameters.
AI.result: The classification index indicates that spectral hardness (E_p,i) is the most discriminative feature, significantly more so than duration (T_90,z), with E_iso also contributing meaningfully. The method accurately classifies historical GRB cases regardless of instrumental era.
AI.conclusion: The new classification tool enhances the understanding of GRB progenitors and will aid in refining future cosmological studies by improving the quality of GRB samples.

title: Cache Hierarchy and Vectorization Analysis of Lindblad Master Equation Simulation for Near-Term Quantum Control
summary: Simulation of open quantum systems via the Lindblad master equation is a computational bottleneck in near-term quantum control workflows, including optimal pulse engineering (GRAPE), trajectory-based robustness analysis, and feedback controller design. For the system sizes relevant to near-term quantum control ($d = 3$ for a single transmon with leakage, $d = 9$ for two-qubit, and $d = 27$ for three-qubit), the dominant cost per timestep is a $(d^2 \times d^2)$ complex matrix-vector multiplication: a $9\times9$, $81\times81$, or $729\times729$ dense matvec, respectively. The working set sizes (1.5 KB, 105 KB, and 8.1 MB) straddle the L1, L2, and L3 cache boundaries of modern CPUs, making this an ideal system for cache-hierarchy performance analysis. We characterize the arithmetic intensity ($\approx 1/2$ FLOP/byte in the large-$d$ limit), construct a Roofline model for the propagation kernel, and systematically vary compiler flags and data layout to isolate the contributions of auto-vectorization, fused multiply-add, and structure-of-arrays (SoA) memory layout. We show that SoA layout combined with -O3 -march=native -ffast-math yields $2$--$4\times$ speedup over scalar array-of-structures baselines, and that -ffast-math is essential for enabling GCC auto-vectorization of complex arithmetic. These results motivate a set of concrete recommendations for authors of quantum simulation libraries targeting near-term system sizes.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses the computational challenges of simulating open quantum systems via the Lindblad master equation, particularly focusing on optimization strategies for matrix operations to enhance performance on modern CPUs.
AI.motivation: To overcome the computational bottlenecks in simulating open quantum systems while performing tasks like optimal pulse engineering and feedback controller design.
AI.method: The study analyzes the performance of matrix-vector multiplications by constructing a Roofline model, examining compiler optimizations, and employing the structure-of-arrays (SoA) layout for enhanced arithmetic intensity and cache usage.
AI.result: Using SoA layout with optimized compiler flags, the research achieves a speedup of 2-4 times compared to traditional methods, highlighting the importance of compiler options like -ffast-math for auto-vectorization.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides practical recommendations for quantum simulation libraries to improve efficiency in simulating near-term quantum systems.

title: Narrowband Radio Technosignature Search toward 3I/ATLAS with FAST
comment: 26 pages, 15 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to AAS Journals
summary: 3I/ATLAS is the third confirmed interstellar object passing through the Solar System. In this work, we conduct narrowband radio technosignature search toward 3I/ATLAS using the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST) L-band multibeam receiver from October 2025 to January 2026 on 4 separate dates (i.e. Mars closest, perihelion, Earth closest and flew away from Earth, respectively). We carry out frequency-drifting signal searching with signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over 10 within 1.05-1.45 GHz via \texttt{bliss} pipeline. These signal hits are grouping into event by beam, frequency and drift rate matching, the events are then filtered by cluster analysis and drift rate cut-off. We also characterized the events by their significance in SNR, structure tensor as well as principal component analysis (PCA). No credible narrowband radio technosignature are detected from 3I/ATLAS after visual inspections. The null results place constraints on the presence of transmitters above $2.862\times 10^{-3}$ W. We further introduce a Bayesian inference framework to constraints on the existence probability and characteristic power of hypothetical transmitters using physically motivated priors to bracket plausible transmitter scenarios.

AI.tldr: The study conducted a narrowband radio technosignature search for interstellar object 3I/ATLAS using FAST, finding no credible signals and placing constraints on potential transmitters.
AI.motivation: To search for signs of extraterrestrial technology associated with interstellar object 3I/ATLAS in the Solar System.
AI.method: Utilized FAST L-band multibeam receiver to conduct frequency-drifting signal searches, employing signal filtering and analysis techniques, including PCA and cluster analysis.
AI.result: No credible narrowband radio technosignatures were detected; null results constrained transmitter power to above $2.862\times 10^{-3}$ W.
AI.conclusion: Introduced a Bayesian inference framework to evaluate existence probabilities and characteristics of potential transmitters.

title: XCOM: Full Mesh Network Synchronization and Low-Latency Communication for QICK (Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit)
summary: Quantum computing experiments and testbeds with large qubit counts have until recently been a privilege afforded only to large companies or quantum technologies where scaling to hundreds or thousands of qubits does not require a substantial increase in quantum control hardware (neutral atoms, trapped ions, or spin defects). Superconducting and spin qubit testbeds critically depend on scaling their control systems beyond what a single electronics board can provide. Multi-board control systems combining RF, fast DC control, bias, and readout require precise synchronization and communication across many hardware and firmware components. To address this, we present XCOM, a network that synchronizes QICK boards and the absolute clocks governing quantum program execution to within 100 ps, free of drift and loss of lock. XCOM also provides deterministic, all-to-all simultaneous data communication with latency below 185 ns. Like QICK itself, XCOM is compatible with a broad range of qubit technologies and is designed to scale to large systems.

AI.tldr: XCOM is a network solution for synchronizing multi-board control systems in quantum computing, achieving precise synchronization and low-latency communication across hardware components.
AI.motivation: There is a need for scalable control systems in superconducting and spin qubit testbeds, which require coordination beyond single electronics board capabilities.
AI.method: XCOM synchronizes QICK boards and absolute clocks to within 100 ps and enables deterministic all-to-all data communication with latency below 185 ns.
AI.result: XCOM achieves high precision and low latency communication for multi-board control in large-scale quantum systems.
AI.conclusion: XCOM is a scalable and versatile solution that enhances the coordination of control systems in diverse qubit technologies.

title: Combined effective field theory interpretation of measurements sensitive to quartic gauge boson couplings in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
comment: 35 pages in total, author list starting page 18, 5 figures, 3 tables, submitted to PLB. All figures including auxiliary figures are available at https://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/PHYSICS/PAPERS/STDM-2023-21/
summary: A combination of measurements sensitive to anomalous quartic electroweak gauge boson couplings is presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV at the LHC. Contributing analyses include measurements of vector-boson scattering in numerous final states as well as a tri-boson measurement. The combined measurement is used to constrain anomalous electroweak boson quartic self-couplings that result from dimension-8 operators in the Éboli model using an effective field theory. Results are presented as 68% and 95% confidence level intervals parameterised by one or two Wilson coefficients, both with and without unitarity constraints applied. Theoretical bounds from unitarity and positivity are overlaid where relevant. Confidence intervals obtained from simultaneous profiled fits to all Wilson coefficients are also presented.

AI.tldr: This paper presents combined measurements of anomalous electroweak gauge boson couplings using ATLAS data, providing constraints on quartic self-couplings from dimension-8 operators in the Éboli model.
AI.motivation: To investigate anomalous quartic couplings of electroweak bosons, which could provide insights into new physics beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: The analysis utilizes proton-proton collision data from the ATLAS detector, focusing on vector-boson scattering and tri-boson measurements, applying effective field theory to constrain the anomalous couplings.
AI.result: Results are expressed as confidence intervals parameterized by Wilson coefficients, indicating the presence or absence of unitarity constraints, with related theoretical bounds noted.
AI.conclusion: This comprehensive analysis enhances the understanding of electroweak interactions and sets limits on new physics scenarios, contributing significant findings to the field.

title: Supermassive Black Hole Winds in X-rays: SUBWAYS V. Properties of hot coronae in quasars at intermediate redshift
summary: We present the X-ray analysis of coronal properties in a statistically representative sample of 23 mostly radio-quiet AGN from the SUBWAYS campaign (SUpermassive Black holes Winds in XrAYs), focusing on quasars at redshifts $0.1 < z < 0.4 $ and bolometric luminosities $2 \times 10^{44} <L_{bol}(erg/s) < 2 \times 10^{46}$. The main aim of this work is to investigate the properties of the hot corona through the study of the hard X-ray band emission, including a proper treatment of the soft X-ray band. High-quality X-ray spectra from XMM-Newton, complemented by NuSTAR data extending up to 30-40 keV in the rest frame, are available for this sample. The soft X-ray band (0.3-2 keV) spectrum is best fitted by a warm corona model with a median temperature of 0.40 keV, and an optical depth in the range $τ$=20 - 40, consistent with previous results on lower luminosity sources. The hard X-ray band is well described using a hot corona model, with a median high-energy cut-off of 87 keV, at the lower end of the distribution of typical values found in Seyfert galaxies (100 - 200 keV). The derived median value of the optical depth ($τ$ = 1 - 5) suggests the presence of a moderately optically thick corona. Combining the SUBWAYS results with literature samples at low and high redshift, we assemble the largest sample to date of AGN with E$_{cut}$ and accretion parameter measurements, finding a significant anticorrelation of E$_{cut}$ with both $λ_{Edd}$ and $L_{bol}$ with the median E$_{cut}$ decreasing from 250 - 300 keV at low accretion rates and luminosities to 90 - 100 keV at high accretion rates and luminosities - consistent with enhanced coronal cooling, possibly driven by pair-production. These results favor cooler, optically thicker coronae in luminous AGN compared to those in lower-luminosity Seyfert galaxies.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the X-ray properties of 23 radio-quiet AGN to examine the characteristics of their hot coronae, finding relationships between the energy cut-off and accretion parameters.
AI.motivation: The aim is to understand the properties of AGN coronae by analyzing hard and soft X-ray emissions in a representative sample of quasars.
AI.method: The research utilized high-quality X-ray spectra from XMM-Newton and NuSTAR, focusing on the emission in the soft (0.3-2 keV) and hard X-ray (up to 30-40 keV) bands.
AI.result: The soft X-ray spectrum indicates a warm corona with a temperature of 0.40 keV and optical depth of 20-40. The hard X-ray band is described by a hot corona model with a median cut-off energy of 87 keV and optical depth of 1-5, showing a significant anti-correlation with accretion parameters.
AI.conclusion: Luminous AGN exhibit cooler and optically thicker coronae compared to lower-luminosity Seyfert galaxies, supporting the notion of enhanced coronal cooling driven by pair-production.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Fast and Robust Longitudinal Qubit Readout
summary:
Longitudinal coupling offers a compelling pathway for quantum nondemolition (QND) readout, but pulse design is constrained by hardware limitations such as the coupling strength and the photon number required to stay within the linear regime.
  We develop a reinforcement learning framework to optimize the longitudinal coupling waveform under such constraints.
  Building upon the theoretical foundation of shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA), we parameterize an auxiliary trajectory with cubic B-splines and reconstruct the physical control.
  At a fixed short readout time, the optimized pulse converges to a constraint saturating flat-top protocol and yields a approximately $50\%$ improvement in $\mathrm{SNR}$ over an STA baseline, while exhibiting enhanced robustness to parameter drifts.
  Simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of reinforcement learning in optimizing longitudinal readout pulses.
  The optimized protocol attains substantial performance gains and yields smooth, hardware-compatible waveforms governed by an interpretable ``saturate-and-hold'' mechanism.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a reinforcement learning approach to optimize longitudinal coupling waveforms for quantum nondemolition readout, improving signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and robustness under hardware constraints.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to enhance quantum nondemolition (QND) readout through optimized pulse design, addressing limitations posed by coupling strength and necessary photon numbers.
AI.method: A reinforcement learning framework is developed to optimize the longitudinal coupling waveform, utilizing shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA) and cubic B-spline parameterization.
AI.result: The optimized pulse achieves a roughly 50% improvement in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to an STA baseline and shows better robustness to parameter drifts.
AI.conclusion: The study successfully demonstrates that reinforcement learning can effectively enhance the performance of longitudinal readout pulses, providing smooth and interpretable waveforms aligned with hardware constraints.

title: D$_4$CNN$\times$AnaCal: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Accurate and Precise Weak Lensing Shear Estimation
comment: 17 pages, 8 figures, and two tables. Submitting to APJ
summary: Traditional weak gravitational lensing shear estimators are carefully calibrated but struggle to fully capture realistic galaxy morphologies, point-spread-function (PSF) effects, blending, and noise in deep surveys, while blindly trained machine learning (ML) models can introduce significant calibration biases. Here we construct a fully D$_4$-equivariant deep neural network for galaxy shape measurement whose architecture enforces symmetry under 90$^{\circ}$ rotations and mirror transformations, and adopt the Analytical Calibration framework (AnaCal) to calibrate the model using its backpropagated gradients. For isolated galaxies in LSST-like single-band simulations, we demonstrate that our approach achieves $\sim$10% lower shape noise than the traditional moment-based Fourier Power Function Shapelets estimator in the high-noise regime, equivalent to a $\sim$20% gain in effective galaxy number density, while simultaneously achieving multiplicative biases consistent with zero across a wide range of noise levels, PSF sizes and ellipticities, and magnitude selection cuts, with all measurements satisfying $|m| {<} 10^{-3}$ (i.e., within the 0.2% LSST requirement) and most at the ${\sim}10^{-4}$ level. We demonstrate this framework on isolated single-band galaxy images with Gaussian noise and known PSF, establishing a rigorous, physics-informed foundation for future extensions of ML-based shear estimation to blended sources and multi-band observations in Stage-IV surveys. All codes and data products will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a D$_4$-equivariant deep neural network for galaxy shape measurement that overcomes calibration biases while achieving lower shape noise and effective density gains compared to traditional methods.
AI.motivation: Traditional weak lensing shear estimators face limitations in capturing realistic galaxy morphologies and biases in machine learning models.
AI.method: A D$_4$-equivariant neural network architecture is used along with the Analytical Calibration (AnaCal) framework for calibration, focusing on isolated galaxies in LSST-like simulations.
AI.result: The proposed method achieves approximately 10% lower shape noise and about 20% increase in effective galaxy number density while maintaining negligible multiplicative biases across varied conditions.
AI.conclusion: The framework sets a strong foundation for future ML-based shear estimation in complex scenarios and will provide publicly available data and codes.

title: Measurement of the $\mathbf{B^0}$-meson production cross section in proton--proton collisions at $\mathbf{\sqrt{\textit{s}}=13.6}$ TeV

summary: This article reports the measurement of the transverse-momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) differential production cross section of B$^0$ mesons in proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV with the ALICE detector at the CERN LHC. Its rapidity dependence is also studied by computing the $p_{\rm T}$-differential ratios between the ALICE measurement and the one of B$^+$ mesons performed by the LHCb Collaboration at forward rapidity.
