title: Neutrinos and gamma rays from Seyfert galaxies constrain the properties of coronal turbulence
summary: The TeV neutrino signal observed by IceCube from the active galactic nucleus (AGN) NGC 1068 can probe its innermost coronal regions. If these neutrinos originate from hadrons accelerated within a magnetized turbulent corona, their intensity and spectrum depend on the turbulent magnetic field strength and turbulence coherence scale. The gamma rays accompanying neutrino production are absorbed in this optically thick environment, in a way that depends sensitively on the size of the corona. By a joint fit of the IceCube and Fermi-LAT observations, we translate the multimessenger signal from NGC 1068 and the tentative signal from NGC 7469 into quantitative constraints on coronal properties. NGC 1068, with a significant TeV neutrino excess, favors a compact, strongly magnetized corona with a large turbulence coherence length relative to the coronal size. NGC 7469, with two $\sim 100$ TeV neutrino events, points instead to a somewhat larger corona with much smaller coherence length and high magnetization, but a very small fraction of energy in non-thermal protons. We obtain the diffuse flux from a population of Seyfert galaxies identical to either NGC 1068 or NGC 7469. Finally, we consider a third scenario, motivated by the spectral break observed in the diffuse neutrino flux at tens of TeV, with coronal properties intermediate between the two point-source-inspired models. To enable detailed comparisons with the IceCube and electromagnetic observations, we release our model predictions in a GitHub repository.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes TeV neutrinos from AGN NGC 1068 and NGC 7469, probing coronal properties through multimessenger signals and fitting IceCube and Fermi-LAT data.
AI.motivation: To understand the coronal properties of AGN based on observed neutrino signals and their implications for hadronic acceleration.
AI.method: Jointly fit neutrino data from IceCube and gamma-ray data from Fermi-LAT, focusing on the relationship between the magnetic field, turbulence, and coronal size.
AI.result: Quantitative constraints on coronal properties are derived, indicating NGC 1068 has a compact, strongly magnetized corona, while NGC 7469 suggests a larger corona with lower non-thermal proton energy.
AI.conclusion: Model predictions are made available for future comparisons, highlighting diverse coronal properties based on neutrino observations.

title: One Key Good, L Keys Better: List Decoding Meets Quantum Privacy Amplification
summary: We introduce list privacy amplification (LPA), a relaxation of the final step of quantum key distribution (QKD) in which Alice and Bob extract a list of $L$ candidate keys from a raw string correlated with an eavesdropper Eve, with the guarantee that at least one key is perfectly secret while Eve cannot identify which. This parallels list decoding in error-correcting codes: relaxing unique decoding to list decoding increases the decoding radius; analogously, list extraction increases achievable key length beyond the standard quantum leftover hash lemma (QLHL). Within the abstract cryptography framework, we formalise LPA and prove the \emph{Quantum List Leftover Hash Lemma} (QLLHL): an $L$-list of $\ell$-bit keys can be extracted from an $n$-bit source with smooth min-entropy $k$ iff \[ \ell \le k + \log L - 2\log(1/ε) - 3, \] yielding a tight additive $\log L$ gain over QLHL. This gain arises because the index of the secure key is chosen after hashing and hidden from Eve, effectively contributing $\log L$ bits of entropy. Applying QLLHL to BB84-type QKD, a list size $L = 2^{αn'}$ increases the tolerable phase-error threshold from $h^{-1}(1 - h(e_b))$ to $h^{-1}(1 - h(e_b) + α)$, exceeding the standard $\approx 11\%$ bound for any $α> 0$. We prove tightness via a matching intercept-resend attack, establish composability with Wegman--Carter authentication, and present two constructions: a polynomial inner-product hash over $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$ and a Toeplitz-based variant, running in $O(nL)$ and $O(nL \log n)$ time.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces list privacy amplification (LPA) to enhance key extraction in quantum key distribution (QKD), ensuring that at least one key remains secret from an eavesdropper while increasing the length of extractable keys.
AI.motivation: To improve the final key extraction step in QKD and address limitations of traditional quantum leftover hash lemma (QLHL) by allowing the extraction of multiple candidate keys while guaranteeing at least one remains secret from an eavesdropper.
AI.method: Formalizes list privacy amplification (LPA) within an abstract cryptographic framework and proves the Quantum List Leftover Hash Lemma (QLLHL) that allows for a list of candidate keys to be extracted under specific conditions, offering an additive gain over QLHL.
AI.result: Establishes that the list size can be increased significantly, allowing for larger tolerable error rates in QKD schemes; demonstrates the conditions under which LPA can be effectively applied, alongside proving its tightness and providing two practical constructions.
AI.conclusion: LPA effectively increases key extraction capabilities in QKD, enabling higher resistance against eavesdropping and larger successful key lengths, with practical constructions that enhance the performance of quantum cryptographic systems.

title: Revisiting Bino-Slepton Coannihilation Dark Matter in Light of Recent Experimental Results
summary: Despite being a simple and well-motivated thermal relic scenario, coannihilation dark matter (DM) has remained largely unexplored experimentally due to the difficulty of probing its nearly degenerate mass spectrum. Recent LHC searches, however, have significantly improved the sensitivity to such compressed spectra, motivating a reassessment of the viable parameter space. We revisit the bino-slepton coannihilation scenario in supersymmetric (SUSY) models, incorporating the latest experimental results. We first focus on the minimal scenario, in which only the bino-like neutralino and left- or right-handed sleptons are light ($O(100)$ GeV), with all other SUSY particles decoupled. We find that the dark matter mass is constrained to be in the range of about 170-420 GeV (130-430 GeV) for left-handed (right-handed) slepton coannihilation, with lower bounds set by recent LHC searches. We then investigate scenarios with light higgsino, where direct detection experiments impose strong constraints on the higgsino mass. We also discuss the implications of these constraints for the muon $g-2$ in the so-called BHR, BHL, and BLR scenarios with coannihilation DM, and find that the combined LHC and LZ limits constrain the SUSY contribution to $|Δa_μ^{\rm SUSY}|\lesssim 1.2\times10^{-9}$.

AI.tldr: The study reassesses the parameter space of coannihilation dark matter in supersymmetric models, focusing on bino-slepton scenarios and incorporating recent LHC results, revealing specific mass constraints and implications for experimental observations.
AI.motivation: To explore the largely unexplored parameter space of coannihilation dark matter, particularly in the context of recent enhancements in LHC sensitivity to compressed mass spectra.
AI.method: The authors analyze the bino-slepton coannihilation scenario using the latest LHC results, focusing on minimal setups with light bino-like neutralinos and sleptons, and extending the analysis to include light higgsinos.
AI.result: The mass of dark matter is constrained to approximately 170-420 GeV for left-handed sleptons and 130-430 GeV for right-handed sleptons, with implications for muon g-2 and the SUSY contribution being limited to |Δa_μ^{m SUSY}|≤1.2×10^{-9}.
AI.conclusion: The combined constraints from LHC and direct detection experiments significantly narrow the viable parameter space for coannihilation dark matter and highlight its implications for related particles and observables.

title: Hyper-efficient superconducting filterbanks with impedance-defined spectral resolution for millimeter-wave spectroscopy
summary: We present a high-efficiency, high resolution on-chip filterbank spectrometer designed for line intensity mapping and broadband wave-like dark matter searches. This spectrometer maximizes sensitivity to the faint, aggregate cosmic signal for line intensity mapping while providing redshift precision necessary to resolve the clustering of large-scale structure. For broadband dark matter searches, it partitions broadband signals into narrow frequency bins that directly correspond to dark matter masses, allowing signal frequency to be mapped with high precision to the particle's mass. Existing superconducting filterbank architectures used by the mm-wave community are limited by a 50\% inherent efficiency limit and are highly sensitive to thin-film dielectric loss. The design presented in this paper addresses these bottlenecks by eliminating the termination resistor and employing a niobium-on-silicon coplanar waveguide resonant structures for the filterbanks. Sonnet electromagnetic simulations of a 10-channel device around 90 GHz demonstrates >74\% per channel efficiency and a resolving power of $R=1211\pm105$. Sensitivity analyses confirm that the design is robust against typical fabrication uncertainties with the exception of dielectric thickness, providing a scalable technology solution for the next generation of millimeter-wave spectroscopic experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a high-efficiency on-chip filterbank spectrometer for line intensity mapping and dark matter searches, overcoming limitations in existing architectures.
AI.motivation: To improve sensitivity and precision in line intensity mapping and broadband dark matter searches, addressing existing efficiency and loss issues in superconducting filterbank designs.
AI.method: The design eliminates the termination resistor and utilizes niobium-on-silicon coplanar waveguide resonant structures, evaluated through Sonnet electromagnetic simulations.
AI.result: Achieved >74% efficiency per channel in a 10-channel device at 90 GHz, with a resolving power of R=1211±105.
AI.conclusion: The design offers a scalable solution for future millimeter-wave spectroscopic experiments, demonstrating robustness against fabrication uncertainties.

title: A systematic search for physical associations between fast radio bursts and astrophysical transients
summary: The physical origin of fast radio bursts (FRBs) remains an unsolved mystery in astrophysics, with the magnetar central engine model as the leading framework. Systematically searching for physical associations between FRBs and the energetic astrophysical transients (ATs) that form magnetars provides a critical test of this scenario, and key clues to FRB progenitors. We perform a systematic search for FRB-AT associations using a sample of 3765 unique FRBs, combining the second CHIME/FRB catalog with 124 additional localized FRBs with measured redshifts. We develop a 3D Bayesian inference framework that jointly incorporates angular separation, positional uncertainty, and redshift constraints to quantify the association probability of candidate pairs. Through spatial cross-matching, we identify 14 FRB-optical transient and 15 FRB-gamma-ray burst (GRB) candidate pairs. Our framework recovers the previously reported high-significance association between FRB 20180916B and AT 2020hur, with an association probability of 0.9998. For the proposed candidate FRB 20190309A and short GRB 060502B, our analysis yields an association probability of 0.83, which is insufficient to claim statistically significant association. No new statistically significant FRB-AT associations are found for all remaining candidates. Our work demonstrates that small angular separation alone is insufficient to confirm FRB-AT associations, and high-precision FRB localization is essential for definitive identification.

AI.tldr: This study investigates associations between fast radio bursts (FRBs) and energetic astrophysical transients (ATs) using Bayesian methods, revealing limited associations and emphasizing the need for precise localization.
AI.motivation: To explore the relationship between FRBs and their potential progenitors, particularly magnetars, by systematically searching for associations with energetic astrophysical transients (ATs).
AI.method: A 3D Bayesian inference framework was employed to assess the association probabilities between 3765 FRBs and ATs, considering angular separation, positional uncertainty, and redshift constraints.
AI.result: Identified 14 FRB-optical transient and 15 FRB-gamma-ray burst candidate pairs; confirmed a strong association for FRB 20180916B with an AT probability of 0.9998, but found no new significant associations for other candidates.
AI.conclusion: While small angular separation is noted, it alone cannot confirm FRB-AT associations, highlighting the importance of high-precision localization for reliable identifications.

title: Improved quantum circuits for division
summary: Arithmetic operations are an important component of many quantum algorithms. As such, coming up with optimized quantum circuits for these operations leads to more efficient implementations of the corresponding algorithms. In this paper, we develop new fault-tolerant quantum circuits for various integer division algorithms (both reversible and non-reversible). These circuits, when implemented in the Clifford+T gate set, achieve an up to 76.08\% and 68.35\% reduction in T-count and CNOT-count, respectively, compared to previous circuit constructions. Some of our circuits also improve the asymptotic T-depth from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n \log n),$ where $n$ is the bit-length of the dividend. The qubit counts are also lower than in previous works. We achieve this by expressing the division algorithms in terms of a primitive we call COMP-N-SUB, that compares two integers and conditionally subtracts them. We show that this primitive can be implemented at a cost, in terms of both Clifford and non-Clifford gates, that is comparable to one addition. This is in contrast to performing comparison and conditional subtraction separately, whose cost would be comparable to a controlled addition plus a regular addition.

AI.tldr: This paper presents optimized fault-tolerant quantum circuits for integer division algorithms, achieving significant reductions in T-count and CNOT-count compared to previous constructions.
AI.motivation: To develop more efficient quantum circuits for arithmetic operations crucial in quantum algorithms.
AI.method: Introducing a primitive called COMP-N-SUB, which combines integer comparison and conditional subtraction, enabling more efficient circuit designs.
AI.result: The new circuits achieved up to 76.08% T-count reduction and 68.35% CNOT-count reduction, and improved asymptotic T-depth from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n "log n)$.
AI.conclusion: This approach lowers both qubit counts and gate costs, enhancing the efficiency of integer division in quantum computing.

title: $d_{N Ω}$ production in $Ωd$ scattering process
summary: In the present work, we propose to investigate the production of $d_{N Ω}$ in the $Ω^{-} d \rightarrow p d_{N Ω}^-$ process by utilizing an effective Lagrangian approach, where $d_{N Ω}$ is identified as $NΩ$ bound state with the binding energy $E_{b}=2.46$ MeV. Experimentally, the J-PARC hadron facility proposed to investigate the $K^{-}p \rightarrow Ω^{-} \bar{K}^{(*)0} K^{+}$ process, which is expected to yield an $Ω$ beam with the momentum of approximately 3 GeV. Additionally, theoretical studies of the $ψ(2S) \rightarrow Ω^{-} \barΩ^{+}$ process at BESIII provided an $Ω$ beam with the momentum of 774 MeV. Considering these two potential $Ω$ beam sources, our estimations show that for the $Ω^{-} d \rightarrow p d_{N Ω}^-$ process, the cross sections are $\Big(329.7^{+26.9}_{-49.6}\Big)$ $μ$b, $\Big(174.0^{+26.5}_{-38.2}\Big)$ $μ$b, $\Big(16.9^{+7.4}_{-7.7}\Big)$ $μ$b, and $\Big(2.0^{+1.8}_{-1.4}\Big)$ $μ$b at $P_Ω =$ 0.7, 0.9, 2.0, and 4.0 GeV, respectively, where the central values are estimated with $Λ_{r}=1.0$ GeV, and the errors come from the variation of $Λ_{r}$ from 0.8 to 1.2 GeV. We also estimate the differential cross sections, which reach the maximum at the forward angle limit. In addition, since the $d_{N Ω}$ dibaryon predominantly decays into $ΞΛ$. Therefore, we further investigate the $Ω^{-} d \rightarrow p Ξ^- Λ$ process and estimate the relevant cross sections. It is expected that the present estimations can be tested by further experimental measurements at J-PARC and STCF in the future.

title: Higgs boson decay to massive bottom quarks at order $α_s^4$ induced by top-quark Yukawa couplings
summary: The Higgs boson decay to massive bottom quarks has the largest branching ratio. The decay is mainly induced by the bottom-quark Yukawa coupling with the decay rate calculated up to $\mathcal{O}(α_s^4)$ assuming the massless final-state bottom quark. The top-quark Yukawa coupling induced contribution starts at $\mathcal{O}(α_s^2)$, and exhibits logarithmic and power enhancements, making the perturbative expansion converge slowly. We present a calculation of such contributions at $\mathcal{O}(α_s^4)$ to the decay into massive bottom quarks in which the squared amplitudes contain two top-quark Yukawa couplings. We find that they increase the decay width, relative to the result up to $\mathcal{O}(α_s^3)$, by $0.4\%$, larger than the experimental precision at future lepton colliders, and reduce the scale dependence significantly down to $0.4\%$.

AI.tldr: The paper calculates contributions to Higgs boson decay to massive bottom quarks, finding that including top-quark Yukawa effects increases the decay width by 0.4%, which surpasses experimental precision at future lepton colliders.
AI.motivation: To improve the accuracy of the decay rate of the Higgs boson to massive bottom quarks by including higher-order contributions from top-quark Yukawa interactions.
AI.method: Calculated the decay width to $	ext{b} ar{	ext{b}}$ at $	ext{O}(α_s^4)$, factoring in contributions from top-quark Yukawa couplings, focusing on their enhancements due to logarithmic and power terms.

AI.conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of top-quark contributions in precision measurements of Higgs boson decay, potentially impacting future experimental observations.

title: GRB 241030A: a bright afterglow challenging forward shock emission
summary: Gamma-Ray Burst GRB 241030A (z = 1.411) exhibited a bright afterglow (similar to GRB 221009A), detected across gamma-ray, X-ray, UV, and optical bands, providing a probe of GRB afterglow physics. We compiled multi-wavelength observations spanning from a minute to a week after the prompt emission, processing the data through a unified photometry pipeline. We analysed the observations both analytically and using Bayesian inference with two independent models. Our models assume that the afterglow emission arises from the strong forward shock of a laterally structured jet, with possible contributions from synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) scatterings. Our models reproduce X-ray to optical data, favouring a jet propagating into a constant-density interstellar medium, with a viewing angle within the jet core. However, both analyses require parameter values that are extreme compared to expectations from standard theory. In particular, our results imply extremely energetic jets despite regular prompt energy, leading to a very inefficient prompt emission. Furthermore, the jets are inefficient at accelerating particles, with low electron and magnetic energy fractions, leading to significant SSC emission. Our analyses indicate that the jets have large opening angles and propagate in high-density media. If the afterglow is indeed powered by radiation emitted behind a strong forward shock, our results place GRB 241030A within a sub-class of GRBs characterised by extreme kinetic energies, large jet opening angles, and very low prompt emission efficiencies, with strong SSC radiation. These predictions are difficult to reconcile with typical expectations from other GRBs. We therefore suggest that the afterglow of GRB 241030A is not solely powered by forward shock emission.

AI.tldr: GRB 241030A shows unusual afterglow characteristics, challenging standard GRB models.
AI.motivation: To investigate the afterglow physics of GRB 241030A and evaluate the implications for jet structure and energy.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength observations analyzed with a unified photometry pipeline and Bayesian inference using models of jet physics affecting afterglows.
AI.result: The study finds that GRB 241030A's jets are energetic yet inefficient with large opening angles, contradicting conventional GRB expectations.
AI.conclusion: The afterglow suggests additional emission mechanisms beyond the forward shock, indicating GRB 241030A fits a unique subclass of GRBs.

title: Towards sample-optimal learning of bosonic Gaussian quantum states
summary: Continuous-variable systems enable key quantum technologies in computation, communication, and sensing. Bosonic Gaussian states emerge naturally in various such applications, including gravitational-wave and dark-matter detection. A fundamental question is how to characterize an unknown bosonic Gaussian state from as few samples as possible. Despite decades-long exploration, the ultimate efficiency limit remains unclear. In this work, we study the necessary and sufficient number of copies to learn an $n$-mode Gaussian state, with energy less than $E$, to $\varepsilon$ trace distance with high probability. We prove a lower bound of $Ω(n^3/\varepsilon^2)$ for Gaussian measurements, matching the best known upper bound up to doubly-log energy dependence, and $Ω(n^2/\varepsilon^2)$ for arbitrary measurements. We further show an upper bound of $\widetilde{O}(n^2/\varepsilon^2)$ given that the Gaussian state is promised to be either pure or passive. Interestingly, while Gaussian measurements suffice for nearly optimal learning of pure Gaussian states, non-Gaussian measurements are provably required for optimal learning of passive Gaussian states. Finally, focusing on learning single-mode Gaussian states via non-entangling Gaussian measurements, we provide a nearly tight bound of $\widetildeΘ(E/\varepsilon^2)$ for any non-adaptive schemes, showing adaptivity is indispensable for nearly energy-independent scaling. As a byproduct, we establish sharp bounds on the trace distance between Gaussian states in terms of the total variation distance between their Wigner distributions, and obtain a nearly tight sample complexity bound for learning the Wigner distribution of any Gaussian state to $\varepsilon$ total variation distance. Our results greatly advance quantum learning theory in the bosonic regimes and have practical impact in quantum sensing and benchmarking applications.

AI.tldr: Characterization of bosonic Gaussian states using minimal samples is studied, revealing necessary sample sizes and bounds for learning these states across various measurements, improving quantum learning theory in practical applications.
AI.motivation: Understanding the efficiency limits in characterizing bosonic Gaussian states is crucial for advancing quantum technologies in diverse fields such as computation and sensing.
AI.method: An analytical approach to determine the number of copies required to learn an n-mode Gaussian state to a defined trace distance, establishing bounds for Gaussian and non-Gaussian measurements.
AI.result: Proved lower bounds of Ω(n^3/ε^2) and Ω(n^2/ε^2) for different measurement types, while deriving upper bounds that indicate the importance of measurement type in learning state properties.
AI.conclusion: The findings enhance the comprehension of quantum learning in bosonic regimes, emphasizing the distinct measurement requirements for pure versus passive Gaussian states, with implications for quantum sensing and benchmarking.

title: Cosmological Implications of the Slingshot Effect: Gravitational Waves, Primordial Black Holes and Dark Matter
comment: 18 pages, 4 figures, ancillary video at https://youtu.be/PnErf4-zUEg
summary: In this paper, we explore the implications of the so-called slingshot effect. It represents a rather general phenomenon occurring when a localized source, such as a monopole, quark, or a $D$-brane, crosses a domain wall separating the confined (Higgsed) and unconfined (Coulomb) phases of the crossing source. The crossover is accompanied by a stretched ``string'' of proper co-dimensionality that confines the source to the domain wall. The effect takes place for different setups, such as phase transitions leading to confinement, both electric and magnetic, as well as in string theoretic inflation with $D$-branes. We discuss the role of the phenomenon in sourcing gravitational waves and dark matter in the form of Kaluza-Klein gravitons. We also show that the slingshot effect can lead to the formation of primordial black holes in observationally interesting mass ranges for dark matter and high-energy cosmic rays.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the slingshot effect, where a localized source crosses a domain wall, affecting gravitational waves, dark matter, and primordial black hole formation.
AI.motivation: To understand the slingshot effect's implications across various physical contexts, including confinement phases and cosmological phenomena.
AI.method: Analysis of the slingshot effect in scenarios involving monopoles, quarks, and $D$-branes crossing domain walls, along with their effects on gravitational waves and dark matter.
AI.result: It demonstrates that the slingshot effect influences gravitational wave sourcing and allows for the creation of primordial black holes within relevant mass ranges for dark matter and cosmic rays.
AI.conclusion: The slingshot effect has significant consequences for cosmology, particularly in the contexts of dark matter and gravitational wave generation.

title: A Systematic Approach to Finite Multiloop Feynman Integrals
summary: Finite Feynman integrals have been advocated as the optimal components for constructing a basis of master integrals in multiloop calculations, due to their improved analytic and numerical properties. In this paper, we show how the Loop-Tree Duality (LTD) is particularly well suited for systematically identifying finite integrals, as it makes the origin of infrared and threshold singularities fully transparent at the integrand level. This clear separation of singular and non-singular contributions enables a more efficient strategy for isolating and promoting finite integrals, thereby streamlining both reduction and numerical evaluation. We present a new strategy based on numerator and raised propagator Ansätze that provides results similar to other methods, although in a clearer and compact way. While this construction and other approaches establish a robust foundation, they often produce integrands that exhibit a rapid growth in the ultraviolet (UV) regime. To mitigate this bad UV behaviour, we introduce a generalized set of integrands fully defined within LTD. This new set is inherently infrared-finite and frequently free of threshold singularities, offering a more versatile framework for high-order calculations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a method using Loop-Tree Duality to identify finite Feynman integrals efficiently, facilitating multiloop calculations by distinguishing singular and non-singular contributions, and introduces a new set of integrands to improve UV behavior.
AI.motivation: To enhance multiloop calculations by leveraging finite Feynman integrals with better analytical and numerical properties.
AI.method: Utilizing Loop-Tree Duality (LTD) to systematically identify finite integrals and propose a new strategy based on numerator and raised propagator Ansätze, alongside a generalized set of integrands defined within LTD.
AI.result: Achieves clarity and compactness in results similar to existing methods, while introducing integrands that are typically infrared-finite and reduce UV issues.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach provides a robust foundation for high-order calculations, offering improved efficiency and management of singularities.

title: Non-Markovian Cosmic-Ray Pitch-Angle Transport from Mirror Interactions
summary: Cosmic-ray pitch-angle transport in magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence is governed by the interplay between magnetic mirroring and gyroresonant scattering. We develop a guiding-center (GC) Langevin model with explicit mirror drift and gyroresonant diffusion to describe the pitch angle evolution. This model accurately captures our test-particle simulation results in three-dimensional MHD turbulence, driven both solenoidally and compressively. We find that magnetic mirroring can drive anomalous pitch-angle diffusion at large pitch angles (including $90^\circ$) with non-Markovian memory effects, which arises from trapping of particles in magnetic wells. Gyroresonant scattering controls the escape rate from these wells. Across $M_{\rm A}$, large-pitch-angle particles are jointly regulated by mirror trapping and gyroresonant escape, exhibiting a transition from anomalous to normal diffusive pitch-angle transport as scattering strengthens, whereas small-pitch-angle particles remain gyroresonance-dominated and diffusive throughout. The pitch angle transport is found to be dominated by the compressible perturbations with marginal influence from Alfvén modes. In compressible turbulence with realistic damping accounted for, transit time damping (TTD) treatment fully recovers mirror interactions.

AI.tldr: The study presents a guiding-center Langevin model for cosmic-ray pitch-angle transport in MHD turbulence, highlighting the roles of magnetic mirroring and gyroresonant scattering.
AI.motivation: To understand cosmic-ray pitch-angle transport influenced by magnetic fields in turbulent plasma environments.
AI.method: A Langevin model incorporating mirror drift and gyroresonant diffusion was developed and validated against test-particle simulations in three-dimensional MHD turbulence.
AI.result: The model shows that magnetic mirroring leads to anomalous pitch-angle diffusion, with significant non-Markovian effects for large-pitch-angle particles, while small-pitch-angle particles exhibit consistent diffusive behavior.
AI.conclusion: The transport mechanism is primarily driven by compressible perturbations, with a notable impact from transit time damping in accounting for mirror interactions.

title: Theory of Two-Qubit $T_2$ Spectroscopy of Quantum Many-Body Systems
summary: Multi-qubit quantum sensors are rapidly emerging as platforms that extend the capabilities of conventional single-qubit sensing. In this work we show how suitable pulse sequences applied to a two-qubit sensor enable separate extraction of the response and noise of a probed environment within a $T_2$ spectroscopy framework. By resorting to representative examples, we demonstrate that this approach can resolve the spatio-temporal spreading of correlations in a many-body system. In particular, the resulting correlated dephasing signal captures features such as the dispersion of low-energy excitations, which manifest as light-cone-like profiles in the propagation of correlations. We further show that non-equilibrium conditions, for instance those induced by external driving, can modify this profile by producing additional fringes outside the light-cone. As a complementary application, we demonstrate that the method clearly distinguishes between different transport regimes in the system, including ballistic spreading, diffusive broadening, and the crossover between them.

AI.tldr: This paper highlights the use of two-qubit quantum sensors to analyze environmental responses and noise through a $T_2$ spectroscopy framework, enabling insights into correlation dynamics and transport regimes.
AI.motivation: To enhance the capabilities of single-qubit sensing by utilizing two-qubit sensors for more nuanced analysis of environmental responses.
AI.method: Suitable pulse sequences are applied to a two-qubit sensor, allowing the separate extraction of response and noise, which enables the resolution of correlation dynamics in many-body systems.
AI.result: The approach successfully resolves spatio-temporal spreading of correlations, revealing features like light-cone-like profiles and the effects of non-equilibrium conditions on these profiles.
AI.conclusion: The method effectively distinguishes between various transport regimes, including ballistic and diffusive behaviors, and demonstrates the potential for profound insights into many-body systems.

title: Probing the Color-Octet Mechanism via Dihadron Fragmentation in $χ_b$ Decays
summary: The color-octet (CO) mechanism is a cornerstone of non-relativistic QCD, yet its long-distance matrix elements remain limited, preventing stringent tests of the theory. We demonstrate that the Artru-Collins asymmetry in hadronic decays of the $P$-wave bottomonium state $χ_{b2}$ provides a direct probe of CO dynamics. The asymmetry arises exclusively from the CO decay channel, whereas the color-singlet (CS) contribution affects only the unpolarized rate, so that a nonzero signal constitutes unambiguous evidence of the CO mechanism. This observable provides a novel way to extract the ratio $ρ_8$ between CO and CS matrix elements. Focusing on $e^+e^-\toΥ(2S)\toγ\,χ_{b2}$ at Belle, we show that the asymmetric beam configuration preserves the asymmetry in the laboratory frame and avoids the strong suppression present in the center-of-mass frame. With the Belle II dataset, $ρ_8$ could be determined with sufficient precision to address the long-standing discrepancy between the lattice calculations and phenomenological determinations.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the Artru-Collins asymmetry in bottomonium decays to investigate the color-octet mechanism in QCD, aiming to resolve discrepancies in matrix element calculations.
AI.motivation: To enhance understanding of color-octet dynamics and address limitations in current QCD matrix element measurements.
AI.method: The Artru-Collins asymmetry in ${e^+e^-}\to Υ(2S)\to γ χ_{b2}$ is analyzed in an asymmetric beam configuration to extract the ratio $ρ_8$ of color-octet to color-singlet matrix elements without strong suppression effects.
AI.result: The proposed method preserves the asymmetry in the laboratory frame, allowing for precise measurements of the ratio $ρ_8$ using data from Belle II.
AI.conclusion: By obtaining a reliable determination of $ρ_8$, the study aims to reconcile discrepancies between lattice calculations and phenomenological results in non-relativistic QCD.

title: GRB 240205B: A Reverse Shock Detected in Rapid Response Radio Observations
summary: Here we present broadband radio modeling of GRB 240205B, using observations with the Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) and the South African MeerKAT radio telescope. Our observations include an automatically triggered early-time ATCA observation that began approximately 13 minutes after the gamma-ray signal and continued for 12 hours, resulting in the earliest detected GRB radio afterglow to date at about 35 minutes post-burst. Following this initial detection, we conducted an extensive radio follow-up campaign for more than 5 months. Although the observations beyond one day post-burst are well described by a standard forward shock model, the observation before one day post-bust reveals an additional synchrotron component, which can be explained as the reverse shock. This component would have been missed without the automated ATCA rapid-response trigger. We find that a combined reverse and forward shock model in a stellar wind medium best describes the radio afterglow. We constrain the spectral breaks due to synchrotron self-absorption and the minimum electron energy, and we use the light-curve peaks to constrain the microphysical parameters. We put GRB 240205B in the context of the growing sample of GRBs with radio detections in the first hours after the gamma-ray trigger. Using our rapid response observation, we estimate the highest model independent constraint on a GRB minimum bulk Lorentz factor of around 100 at about 35 minutes post burst. We also discuss future prospects of detecting similar long GRBs at centimeter wavelengths, as well as potential improvements to future strategies for targeting their radio afterglows.

AI.tldr: This study presents significant radio observations of GRB 240205B, revealing the earliest afterglow detection and introducing key models involving reverse and forward shocks.
AI.motivation: To refine understanding of gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglows, particularly at early times, and to improve detection strategies for future observations.
AI.method: Utilized broadband radio modeling with data from ATCA and MeerKAT, including a rapid-response observation triggered shortly after the GRB, followed by extensive follow-up for over five months.
AI.result: The early radio afterglow indicated a reverse shock component, which is critical for modeling, and provided the highest independent constraint on the GRB's minimum bulk Lorentz factor.
AI.conclusion: A combined shock model effectively describes GRB 240205B's afterglow; the study emphasizes the importance of fast-response observations and outlines strategies for future detections.

title: Fully selective charging of a quantum battery by a purely quantum charger
summary: In this paper we discuss a protocol for charging a two-level quantum battery using a bipartite charger composed of two quantum harmonic oscillators. As one of its features, it allows us to fully charge the battery and is universally optimal in the regime of a single excitation added as energy input. We also make use of a selective interaction to extend the protocol for a different class of quantum states and show that, in this case, the presence of quantum coherence can be harnessed as energetic resource to charge multiple similar batteries. Among these, we also explore symmetries of the derived effective dynamics to quickly discuss how the same protocol can be adapted to the task of \textit{active state resetting}, a task which is particularly useful in the quantum computation area.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an optimal protocol for charging a two-level quantum battery using a bipartite charger, extending its application to multiple batteries by leveraging quantum coherence.
AI.motivation: To optimize the charging efficiency of quantum batteries and explore applications in quantum computation.
AI.method: Introducing a bipartite charger made of quantum harmonic oscillators and selective interactions to charge the battery and adapt protocols for active state resetting.
AI.result: The protocol enables full charging of the battery and is universally optimal; quantum coherence is utilized to charge multiple batteries efficiently.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest significant implications for quantum technology, particularly in quantum computation tasks like active state resetting.

title: Electroweak phase transitions in a $U(1)_D$ extension of the standard model with dimension-six operators: Gravitational waves and LHC signatures
summary:
We investigate the possibility of realizing strong first-order electroweak phase transition (SFOEWPT) in an effective field theory framework where the Standard Model is extended with a complex scalar singlet ($φ$) charged under a local $U(1)_D$ gauge group. The tree-level scalar potential contains a dimension-six term of the form $|H|^2|φ|^4$. We show that this higher-dimensional operator plays a crucial role in the phase transition dynamics by weakening the correlation between the Higgs-singlet portal coupling and the scalar mixing angle that typically constrains singlet-extended models. Consequently, SFOEWPT can be achieved over a significantly extended region of parameter space. The strength of the phase transition is primarily driven by the vacuum expectation value (VEV) of the singlet scalar which plays a central role in this analysis.
  We analyze the phase transition in this model and identify regions of parameter space consistent with SFOEWPT. The resulting phase transition can generate stochastic gravitational-wave signals potentially observable at future interferometers. The extended scalar sector in presence of the dimension-six operator also leads to distinctive multi-scalar production signatures at the LHC, intimately correlated with the singlet scalar VEV.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a model with a complex scalar singlet that enhances first-order electroweak phase transition (SFOEWPT) through a dimension-six operator, allowing for a wider parameter range and linking to observable gravitational waves and LHC signatures.
AI.motivation: To understand SFOEWPT within an effective field theory framework that modifies the Standard Model, enhancing its predictive power for phase transition dynamics.
AI.method: The study involves analyzing a model with a complex scalar singlet and a dimension-six term in the scalar potential, assessing its implications on phase transition parameters and dynamics.
AI.result: The presence of the dimension-six operator significantly expands the parameter space enabling SFOEWPT, predominantly influenced by the singlet scalar's VEV, which also affects particle production at the LHC.
AI.conclusion: This model has the potential to produce observable gravitational waves and distinctive multi-scalar signatures at LHC, indicating significant implications for exploring new physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Transverse spin effects and light-quark dipole moments at colliders
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures. Proceedings for the 26th International Symposium on Spin Physics (SPIN2025), September 21-26, 2025, Qingdao (Tsingtao), Shandong, China
summary: In this talk, we present novel methods to investigate light-quark dipole interactions at colliders. Our approach includes: (1) measuring azimuthal asymmetries of a collinear dihadron in semi-inclusive deep inelastic lepton scattering off an unpolarized proton target at the Electron-Ion Collider, and (2) utilizing azimuthal asymmetries of dihadron $(h_1 h_2)$ produced in association with an additional hadron $h^\prime$ at lepton colliders. These asymmetries provide a unique means to observe transversely polarized quarks, which arise from quantum interference and are exclusively sensitive to dipole interactions at the leading power of the new physics scale. Consequently, they exhibit a linear dependence on the dipole couplings, free from contamination by other new physics effects. This approach has the potential to significantly strengthen current constraints by one to two orders of magnitude. By combining all possible channels of $h^\prime$, this novel approach enables the disentanglement of the up- and down-quark dipole moments. Additionally, by controlling the electron's longitudinal polarization and the center-of-mass energy, it separates the contributions mediated by photon and weak boson. Furthermore, it allows for a simultaneous determination of both real and imaginary parts of the dipole couplings, offering a new avenue for investigating potential $CP$-violating effects at high energies.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces innovative methods to study light-quark dipole interactions at colliders by measuring azimuthal asymmetries in dihadron production, allowing for substantial constraints on quark dipole moments and insights into $CP$ violations.
AI.motivation: To provide a unique and precise methodology for observing transversely polarized quarks and investigating new physics through dipole interactions in collider experiments.
AI.method: Measurement of azimuthal asymmetries in semi-inclusive deep inelastic lepton scattering and dihadron production at lepton colliders, focusing on the interactions of light quarks and their dipole moments.
AI.result: This approach can enhance constraints on dipole couplings by one to two orders of magnitude, facilitating the separation of up- and down-quark dipole moments and the contributions from different mediators.
AI.conclusion: The methods allow for simultaneous determination of dipole couplings, offering a promising route to explore potential $CP$-violating effects at high energies.

title: G objects as Primordial Black Hole-Neutron Star Remnants: Population Modeling and Multi-Wavelength Observables
summary: The nature of the so-called G objects orbiting the Galactic Center remains unresolved. These sources exhibit compact Br$γ$ emission, extreme infrared colors, and remarkable dynamical stability through close passages to the central supermassive black hole, challenging conventional interpretations as stars or unbound gas clouds. We investigate the hypothesis that G objects are the remnants of neutron stars that have been converted into low-mass black holes through the capture of primordial black holes, a viable dark-matter candidate. We construct a population-level framework linking the abundance and spatial distribution of these remnants to the neutron-star population, the inner dark-matter density profile, and the primordial black-hole mass and abundance. Within this framework, the observed G-object population and the long-standing deficit of ordinary radio pulsars in the Galactic Center emerge as complementary consequences of the same conversion process. We further identify a suite of observational signatures-across infrared, radio, X-ray, and microlensing channels-that render this scenario empirically testable and distinguishable from stellar-envelope models. Our results show that G objects can act as sensitive probes of compact-object capture physics and of dark matter on sub-galactic scales.

AI.tldr: G objects near the Galactic Center may be remnants of neutron stars turned into black holes via primordial black hole capture, offering insights into dark matter and compact-object physics.
AI.motivation: To resolve the mystery of G objects, which defy traditional interpretations as stars or gas clouds.
AI.method: A population-level framework relating the characteristics of G objects to neutron-star populations and primordial black holes.
AI.result: G objects and the lack of ordinary radio pulsars in the Galactic Center can be explained by the same conversion process; they provide testable observational signatures across multiple wavelengths.
AI.conclusion: G objects serve as probes for understanding compact-object capture physics and dark matter dynamics on sub-galactic scales.

title: Towards spintronics via tunneling through asymmetric barriers
summary: Spin transport typically relies on direct manipulation of the spin degree of freedom via magnetic fields, spin-orbit coupling, or engineered spin-dependent potentials. We show theoretically that directional spin currents can arise in a relatively simple setting - a one-dimensional interacting fermionic ring with static, spin-independent asymmetric barriers. By introducing asymmetric potential barrier geometry, spin-resolved circulating currents emerge on a closed chain even for symmetric initial configurations. The effect can be enhanced or reversed by appropriate initial state preparation and tuning the barrier asymmetry to resonant conditions.

AI.tldr: Directional spin currents can be generated in a one-dimensional fermionic ring with static, spin-independent asymmetric barriers, showing that initial state preparation and barrier tuning can enhance or reverse these currents.
AI.motivation: The study aims to explore new mechanisms for generating spin transport without relying on conventional methods like magnetic fields or spin-orbit coupling.
AI.method: The authors theoretically analyze a one-dimensional interacting fermionic ring with asymmetric barriers to investigate the emergence of spin-resolved circulating currents.
AI.result: Asymmetric barrier geometries lead to the emergence of spin-resolved currents even from symmetric initial configurations, with the effects being tunable through initial state preparation and barrier adjustments.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest a novel approach to generating directional spin currents, opening avenues for manipulation and control in spintronic devices.

title: Signatures of the $Ω(2012)^{-}$ state in $Ξ^*\bar K$ Correlation Functions
summary:
We investigate the $Ω(2012)$ resonance in the strangeness $S=-3$ sector within a coupled-channel chiral unitary approach and present the first quantitative predictions for femtoscopic correlation functions directly sensitive to its dynamics. The $Ω(2012)$ is dynamically generated as a quasi-bound $Ξ^{\ast}\bar K$-$Ωη$ molecular state, with its coupling to the $Ξ\bar{K}$ channel driven by $d$-wave transitions. Model parameters are constrained by the measured mass, width, and the Belle determination of the branching fraction $\mathcal R^{Ξ\bar Kπ}_{Ξ\bar K}$, yielding $M_{Ω(2012)}=(2012.53\pm0.73)$ MeV and $Γ_{Ω(2012)}=(4.05\pm0.13)$ MeV.
  Within this framework, we compute the femtoscopic correlation functions of the $Ξ^{\ast0}K^-$, $Ξ^{\ast-}\bar K^0$, and $Ω^-η$ systems. The $Ξ^{\ast}\bar K$ correlation functions exhibit pronounced near-threshold structures that arise from the proximity of the $Ω(2012)$ pole, demonstrating an exceptional sensitivity to its position and coupled-channel composition. In particular, the $Ξ^{\ast0}K^-$ correlation function is identified as a clean and highly selective probe of the $Ω(2012)$ resonance. These results establish femtoscopic correlation measurements as powerful tools for extracting resonance properties beyond conventional invariant-mass analyses and provide concrete theoretical benchmarks for upcoming experimental studies aimed at elucidating the molecular nature of the $Ω(2012)$.

AI.tldr: This study presents a quantitative analysis of the $Ω(2012)$ resonance in the strangeness $S=-3$ sector using a coupled-channel chiral unitary approach, highlighting its characteristics through femtoscopic correlation functions.
AI.motivation: To explore the properties of the $Ω(2012)$ resonance, including its dynamics and coupling in the $S=-3$ strangeness sector, and to utilize femtoscopic correlation functions as a means to extract resonance features.
AI.method: The $Ω(2012)$ is modeled as a quasi-bound state within a coupled-channel chiral unitary framework, with parameters constrained by mass and branching fraction measurements. Femtoscopic correlation functions are computed for systems involving $Ξ^{	ext{*}}K^-$, $Ξ^{	ext{*}} ar K^0$, and $Ω^-η$.
AI.result: The $Ω(2012)$ mass is determined to be $(2012.53	ext{meV} 	ext{±} 0.73)$ and its width $(4.05	ext{meV} 	ext{±} 0.13)$. Correlation functions exhibit significant near-threshold features indicative of the $Ω(2012)$ pole, particularly the $Ξ^{	ext{*}}K^-$ function as a selective probe of the resonance.
AI.conclusion: Femtoscopic measurements offer a robust means of probing resonance properties, surpassing traditional analyses and setting a theoretical framework for future experimental investigations of the molecular nature of the $Ω(2012)$.

title: The impact of prescriptions in phenomenological extractions of Transverse Momentum Dependent distributions
summary: We investigate the impact of phenomenological prescriptions in the Collins-Soper-Sterman (CSS) approach for global extractions of Transverse Momentum Distributions (TMDs). We show that fits to low-energy Drell-Yan data with different choices of $b_*$ prescription yield equally good agreement with data and similar TMDs at small partonic transverse momentum. In contrast, sizable differences emerge at intermediate transverse momentum region, significantly affecting the predictions for high-energy Drell-Yan processes. Our results demonstrate that the $b_*$ prescription represents an intrinsic source of theoretical uncertainty in the CSS approach, introducing systematic effects that influence TMD extractions and their interpretation. At the same time, our analysis emphasizes the interplay between data at different energy scales in assessing the effect of phenomenological prescriptions in TMD fits adopting the CSS framework.

AI.tldr: This study examines the impact of phenomenological prescriptions in the CSS approach on TMD extractions, highlighting significant theoretical uncertainties in fits for Drell-Yan data.
AI.motivation: To understand the effects of different $b_*$ prescriptions on the extraction of TMDs using the CSS approach, particularly in relation to Drell-Yan processes.
AI.method: We performed fits to low-energy Drell-Yan data utilizing various $b_*$ prescriptions and analyzed the impact on TMD extractions at different transverse momentum scales.
AI.result: Different $b_*$ prescriptions yielded comparable fits at low energies, but significant differences were observed at intermediate transverse momentum, affecting high-energy predictions.
AI.conclusion: The $b_*$ prescription introduces a theoretical uncertainty in the CSS approach, impacting TMD extractions, and emphasizes the significance of data across energy scales.

title: Dissipative Phase Transition in a Parametrically Amplified Quantum Rabi Model with Two-photon decay
summary: We investigate dissipative phase transitions (DPTs) in a parametrically amplified open quantum Rabi model (QRM) with both single- and two-photon decay. In the classical oscillator limit, four composite phases emerge, arising from the possible normal or superradiant regimes across the upper and lower spin branches. A mean-field analysis reveals an ``inverted" regime where superradiance emerges only at sufficiently low spin-boson coupling. This regime features first- and second-order DPTs separated by a tricritical point, while two-photon dissipation preserves the stability of the superradiant phase. Utilizing an adiabatic approach and the semi-classical Langevin formalism, we further study the steady-state structure beyond the mean-field level. We show that the tricriticality stems from the intrinsic nonlinearity of QRM, unveiled by the interplay of coherent and dissipative two-photon processes. The universality classes of the DPTs are identified, with the corresponding critical and finite-size scaling exponents derived and a scaling ansatz proposed to describe the critical behavior.

AI.tldr: The study explores dissipative phase transitions in an open quantum Rabi model, revealing four composite phases and an inverted regime with distinct DPT characteristics.
AI.motivation: To understand dissipative phase transitions in quantum systems, focusing on their behavior in open quantum Rabi models influenced by photon decay.
AI.method: Mean-field analysis, adiabatic approach, and semi-classical Langevin formalism to analyze steady-state structures and phase transitions.
AI.result: Four composite phases are identified, with a unique inverted regime and a tricritical point marking first- and second-order DPTs, influenced by two-photon dissipation.
AI.conclusion: The findings unveil the role of nonlinearity in criticality and propose scaling relations for understanding the critical behavior of these phase transitions.

title: Hidden-charm pentaquarks: Electromagnetic structure in a diquark--diquark--antiquark model
comment: 15 pages, 2 figure, 4 Tables. . Matches version accepted for publication in EPJC
summary: We systematically investigate the electromagnetic properties of exotic states whose internal structures remain uncertain and for which different models have been proposed. In this work, we focus on the magnetic dipole moments of hidden-charm pentaquark states using QCD light-cone sum rules with four distinct interpolating currents. The analysis accounts for contributions from both light and charm quark sectors, as well as higher-dimensional operators, ensuring convergence of the operator product expansion and dominance of the ground-state pole. Our results demonstrate a strong dependence of the magnetic moments on the internal quark configurations and spin alignments, revealing substantial variations among the different currents despite identical quark content and quantum numbers. Comparisons with existing studies indicate that while molecular-type predictions show general agreement, compact configurations yield markedly different values, including significant differences in sign and magnitude. These findings therefore underscore the sensitivity of electromagnetic observables to the internal structure of exotic hadrons and highlight their potential as probes to discriminate between competing structural models for spin-parity assignments and underlying quark dynamics.

AI.tldr: The study investigates the magnetic dipole moments of hidden-charm pentaquarks using QCD light-cone sum rules, revealing how these moments vary significantly based on internal quark configurations and spin alignments.
AI.motivation: To understand the electromagnetic properties of exotic hadrons and the impact of their internal structures on observables like magnetic dipole moments.
AI.method: Employing QCD light-cone sum rules with four different interpolating currents, accounting for contributions from light and charm quarks and higher-dimensional operators.
AI.result: The magnetic moments exhibit a strong dependence on quark configurations and spin alignments, showing significant variations across different currents despite identical quark content. Molecular-type predictions align with existing studies, while compact configurations present notable disparities in values.
AI.conclusion: Electromagnetic observables are highly sensitive to the internal structure of exotic hadrons, making them effective for distinguishing among different structural models.

title: On Non-Existence of Stabilizer Absolutely Maximally Entangled States in Even Local Dimensions
summary: We demonstrate that absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states consisting of $N=4k$ qudits with $k\in\mathbb{N}_+$, each of even local dimension, cannot be realized as graph states. This result imposes strong constraints on AME states in composite local dimensions and characterizes the limitations of graph-state constructions for highly entangled multipartite quantum systems. In particular, this study provides an independent solution of the recently discussed case of the AME state of four quhexes and clarifies its characterization within the stabilizer formalism, complementing the results of Cha [arXiv:2603.13442].

AI.tldr: The paper shows that AME states with $N=4k$ qudits and even local dimension cannot be graph states, highlighting constraints on multipartite systems.
AI.motivation: To explore the realizability of AME states as graph states and understand their limitations in quantum systems.
AI.method: The authors analyse properties of AME states and their characterization within the stabilizer formalism, using combinatorial and algebraic techniques.
AI.result: Demonstrated that specific AME states (for $N=4k$ qudits) cannot be represented as graph states, impacting our understanding of multipartite entanglement.
AI.conclusion: This work clarifies that certain AME states cannot be constructed as graph states, providing insights into the nature of entanglement in complex quantum systems.

title: Correlator of heavy-light quark currents in HQET in the large $β_0$ limit
comment: A conference talk based on the second half of arXiv:2411.11080
summary: The perturbative contribution to the correlator of two heavy-light quark currents in HQET expanded in light-quark masses up to quadratic terms is calculated at the leading order in $1/β_0$. Ultraviolet and infrared renormalon poles of Borel images of the Wilson coefficients are discussed.

AI.tldr: The paper calculates the perturbative contribution to the correlator of heavy-light quark currents in HQET, focusing on light-quark mass effects and leading-order renormalon poles.
AI.motivation: To enhance the understanding of heavy-light quark currents in the context of Heavy Quark Effective Theory (HQET) and the impact of light-quark mass on their correlators.
AI.method: The authors perform a perturbative expansion in light-quark masses up to quadratic terms and analyze the correlator of heavy-light quark currents at leading order in the parameter $1/β_0$.
AI.result: The study reveals details about ultraviolet and infrared renormalon poles associated with the Borel images of the Wilson coefficients, highlighting the complexities introduced by light-quark mass contributions.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide insight into the structure of heavy-light quark current correlators in HQET and the implications of renormalon behavior in quantum field theories.

title: A global analysis of Energy-Energy Correlation data: determination of $α_S$ and non-perturbative QCD parameters
summary: We present a comprehensive global analysis of Energy-Energy Correlation (EEC) data in electron-positron annihilation into hadrons, spanning a wide range of center-of-mass energies ($7.7\,\,\text{GeV}\!\leq\!\sqrt{s}\!\leq\! 91.2\,\,\text{GeV})$. In the back-to-back (two-jet) region, we resum to all orders the logarithmically-enhanced contributions up to next-to-next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic (N$^3$LL) accuracy. The resummed results are consistently matched to fixed-order calculations up to $\mathcal{O}(α_S^3)$. Our resummation formalism also incorporates dominant heavy-quark mass effects and models non-perturbative power corrections by means of an analytic dispersive approach. A simultaneous fit yields an excellent description of experimental data across all energies, enabling a precise determination of the strong coupling, $α_S(m_Z^2) = 0.119 \pm 0.002$, as well as the non-perturbative parameters, including those characterizing the Collins--Soper evolution kernel. Our analysis includes, for the first time in a global fit, datasets from the ALEPH and AMY collaborations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a detailed analysis of Energy-Energy Correlations in electron-positron annihilation, achieving high precision in determining the strong coupling constant and non-perturbative parameters.
AI.motivation: To analyze Energy-Energy Correlation data in electron-positron annihilation to enhance understanding of strong interactions across varying energies.
AI.method: The authors employ a resummation technique to all orders for logarithmically-enhanced contributions, matching it with fixed-order calculations while including heavy-quark mass effects and non-perturbative corrections.
AI.result: An excellent fit to experimental data was achieved, leading to a precise determination of the strong coupling constant, α_S(m_Z^2) = 0.119 ± 0.002, and characterization of non-perturbative parameters.
AI.conclusion: The analysis, integrating datasets from ALEPH and AMY collaborations, represents a significant advancement in the precision measurement of strong interaction dynamics.

title: Bell-EPR Correlations within Local Quantum Theory
summary: We present a local unitary theory of a Bell-EPR measurement, starting with the premeasurement filtering of the individual photon polarizations and extending through the detection process involving four photodetectors, two at each receiving station. The essential feature is that decoherence occurs locally and independently with each detector upon its absorption of a photon. Communication between observers after they read their local outcomes confirms the known Bell-EPR correlations. This theory is manifestly local, but there exist other formulations, and interpretations, that are non-local.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a local unitary theory for Bell-EPR measurements, detailing premeasurement filtering and the detection process using multiple photodetectors. It highlights local decoherence and the confirmation of Bell-EPR correlations through communication of outcomes.
AI.motivation: To provide a local framework for understanding Bell-EPR measurements amidst various interpretations.
AI.method: The theory incorporates local decoherence linked to each detector's absorption of photons, using four photodetectors positioned at two stations.
AI.result: Local decoherence occurs independently at each detector, aligning with Bell-EPR correlations observed through post-measurement communication.
AI.conclusion: The proposed theory maintains a local perspective, contrasting with other non-local interpretations.

title: Gamma-ray production in the cosmic-ray -- dark matter scattering as a probe of the axion-like particle -- proton interaction
summary: The production of very-high-energy (VHE, $E_γ \gtrsim 100$ GeV) gamma rays resulting from the scattering of high-energy cosmic-ray protons off axion-like particles (ALPs) populating the dark matter halo of the Milky Way is investigated. By employing the latest instrument response functions for current and future facilities, we demonstrate that ground-based VHE gamma-ray observatories, such as H.E.S.S., CTAO, and SWGO, provide a promising and complementary avenue to probe the yet uncharted ALP-proton coupling $g_{ap}$. Our results show that these experiments can reach sensitivity to couplings above $10^{-2}$ in the $1 - 10^{8}$ eV ALP mass range, a region that remains largely unexplored by supernova and neutron star cooling observations. Interestingly, we demonstrate that this search channel is capable of probing QCD axion dark matter models, assuming two benchmark models for it: the Kim-Shifman-Vainshtein-Zakharov (KSVZ) Dine-Fischler-Srednicki-Zhitnitsky (DFSZ) models, specifically within the MeV mass range. These findings highlight the potential of VHE gamma-ray astronomy to provide unique constraints on the interaction between ALPs and the baryonic sector.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the potential of very-high-energy (VHE) gamma-ray observatories to investigate axion-like particles (ALPs) in the Milky Way's dark matter halo through ALP-proton scattering. Current instruments can probe previously unexplored couplings and regions of axion dark matter models.
AI.motivation: To identify and explore the interaction between axion-like particles (ALPs) and cosmic rays, particularly in the context of dark matter interactions within the Milky Way.
AI.method: Utilizing the latest instrument response functions from ground-based VHE gamma-ray observatories like H.E.S.S., CTAO, and SWGO to explore ALP-proton couplings throughout a specified mass range.
AI.result: The study finds that ongoing and future VHE gamma-ray experiments can achieve sensitivities to ALP-proton couplings above $10^{-2}$ in the mass range of $1 - 10^{8}$ eV, revealing the potential to investigate QCD axion dark matter models.
AI.conclusion: VHE gamma-ray astronomy holds significant promise for placing unique constraints on ALPs and their interactions with baryonic matter, thereby advancing our understanding of dark matter.

title: Finite-size resource scaling for learning quantum phase transitions with fidelity-based support vector machines
summary: Quantum kernels offer a valid procedure for learning quantum phase transitions on quantum processing devices, yet issues on the scalability of the learning strategy in connection with the symmetry of the critical model have not been clarified. We derive a link between model symmetry and fidelity-kernel resource scaling. We quantify the measurement resources required to estimate fidelity-based quantum kernels for many-body ground states while preserving the structure of the resulting Gram matrix under finite-shot sampling. Crucially, we show that increasing symmetry in the underlying spin model systematically amplifies these shot requirements. Moving from the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric Ising/XY regimes to the $U(1)$-symmetric XX (and XXZ) regimes leads to stronger kernel concentration and therefore substantially larger shot costs under the same bounds. We consider a tunable one-dimensional spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ Hamiltonian spanning the transverse-field Ising, XY, XX, and XXZ limits, and define the kernel as the ground-state fidelity. Kernel entries are estimated using a SWAP-test estimator with $S$ shots, and we adapt the ensemble spread and concentration-avoidance shot bounds to obtain practical shot requirements in terms of the interquartile range of kernel values and a representative kernel magnitude. For the free-fermion XY/XX family, we use the closed-form Bogoliubov-angle fidelity, while for the interacting XXZ chain we compute fidelities by exact diagonalization and benchmark shot-noise effects. Our symmetry-aware bounds provide a pragmatic procedure for physics-informed quantum machine learning.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the scalability of quantum kernels in learning about quantum phase transitions, addressing how model symmetry affects resource requirements for fidelity estimation.
AI.motivation: To clarify the relationship between model symmetry and the scalability of learning strategies in quantum phase transitions.
AI.method: The authors derive a connection between model symmetry and the required measurement resources, using a tunable one-dimensional spin-1/2 Hamiltonian and estimating fidelity-based quantum kernels via a SWAP-test estimator.
AI.result: Increased symmetry in the spin model leads to higher measurement shot requirements, with specific examples from symmetric Ising, XY, and XXZ regimes illustrating substantial shot costs despite similar bounds.
AI.conclusion: The findings offer a practical framework for implementing physics-informed quantum machine learning by providing symmetry-aware bounds for estimating quantum kernel resources.

title: From N- to (p,N)- Inflationary Attractors in view of ACT
comment: Prepared for the Proceedings of Workshop ''Tensions in Cosmology'' 2 - 8 September 2025 Corfu, Greece - Conference C25-09-02.1
summary: We review two types of fractional Kaehler potentials $K$ which reduce, along the inflationary path, to the form $N/(1-φ^{q_{\rm M}})^{p}$ with $q_{\rm M}=1$ or $2$ and $0.1\leq p\leq10$. Their coexistence, within a non-linear sigma model, with chaotic inflationary potentials of the form $φ^n$ (where $n=2$ or $4$) determines, independently from $q_{\rm M}$ and $n$, a class of $(p,N)$-inflationary attractors which leads to observables compatible with the ACT DR6. An implementation of these models in the context of supergravity can be also achieved by introducing two chiral superfields and a monomial superpotential, linear with respect to the inflaton-accompanying field, and supplementing the $K$'s above with a shift symmetry. Although inflation is attained for subplanckian inflaton values, the tensor-to-scalar ratio obtained for certain $N$ values can be possibly observable in the near future.

AI.tldr: The paper reviews fractional Kaehler potentials in the context of inflation models, identifying attractors leading to observable effects compatible with empirical data.
AI.motivation: To explore the behavior of fractional Kaehler potentials under inflationary dynamics and their impact on observable cosmological parameters.
AI.method: Analyzed two types of fractional Kaehler potentials within a non-linear sigma model alongside traditional chaotic inflationary potentials, employing supergravity models with chiral superfields.
AI.result: Identified a class of inflationary attractors that yield observable predictions consistent with ACT DR6 data, despite inflation occurring at subplanckian inflaton values.
AI.conclusion: The inflation models suggest that the tensor-to-scalar ratio could be measurable soon, as they align with observational data.

title: Searching for dark matter X-ray lines from the Large Magellanic Cloud with eROSITA
summary: We perform a search for an X-ray monochromatic line arising from dark matter (DM) decay in the halo of the Large Magellanic Cloud. An emission line can be expected from two well-motivated DM candidates: sterile neturinos and axion-like particles (ALPs). We analyze the eROSITA-DE DR1 datasets in the energy range between 1 and 9 keV. No evidence for a DM line is found, and we set lower limits on the DM lifetime. We then recast these bounds into upper limits on the active-sterile neutrino mixing angle $\sin^2(2θ)$ and on the ALP to photon coupling $g_{aγ}$, for DM masses between 2 and 18 keV. These results set new strong constraints for masses below 5 keV.

AI.tldr: This study searches for an X-ray line from dark matter decay in the Large Magellanic Cloud, finding no evidence and setting new limits on dark matter properties.
AI.motivation: To explore potential signals of dark matter decay, specifically from sterile neutrinos and axion-like particles, within astronomical observations.
AI.method: Analyzed eROSITA-DE DR1 datasets in the 1 to 9 keV energy range to search for dark matter decay emission lines.
AI.result: No evidence for a dark matter emission line was found, leading to the establishment of lower limits on dark matter lifetime and upper limits on mixing angles and coupling coefficients for specific dark matter candidates.
AI.conclusion: The results provide strong constraints on dark matter mass and properties, particularly for masses below 5 keV.

title: High-dimensional quantum communication with scalable photonic entanglement in time and frequency
summary: High-dimensional photonic entanglement holds significant promise for advancing quantum communication, computation, and metrology. For example, large-alphabet quantum communication protocols are known to benefit from enhanced noise resilience and information capacity via multi-bit time-bin encoding. Yet, characterizing high-dimensional entangled states is challenging, as full state tomography becomes prohibitively costly and often requires unrealizable measurements. Here, we demonstrate a scan-free method to characterize high-dimensional entanglement in the time-frequency domain. Our reconstruction achieves a record $5.70\pm0.07$ ebits and a fidelity of $65.4\pm0.4\%$ with the maximally entangled state of local dimension $1021$, certifying the presence of $668$-dimensional entanglement. We further prove the attainability of a secure key rate of $15.6$ kB/s in a composable finite-size, entanglement-based protocol, and show that in continuous operation, the setup can quickly approach asymptotic key rates. Using commercial telecom components and state-of-the-art low-jitter single-photon detectors, our scalable architecture offers a practical path towards high-rate, noise-resilient quantum communication testbeds.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a scan-free method for characterizing high-dimensional photonic entanglement, achieving notable fidelity and ebit values while paving the way for robust quantum communication.
AI.motivation: The need for improved methods to characterize high-dimensional entangled states due to the limitations of traditional full state tomography.
AI.method: A novel scan-free technique was applied in the time-frequency domain to reconstruct high-dimensional entangled states, achieving notably high fidelity and ebit values.
AI.result: A record $5.70\pm0.07$ ebits with $65.4\pm0.4\%$ fidelity, certifying $668$-dimensional entanglement and enabling a secure key rate of $15.6$ kB/s in a quantum communication protocol.
AI.conclusion: The proposed architecture is both scalable and practical for high-rate, noise-resilient quantum communication schemes, potentially enhancing current capabilities.

title: Preprocessing noise in finite-size quantum key distribution
summary: It is known that preprocessing noise may boost quantum key distribution by expanding the range of values of tolerated noise. For BB84, adding trusted noise may allow the generation of secret keys even for qubit error rate (QBER) beyond the 11% threshold in the asymptotic regime. Here we study the effect of preprocessing noise in the finite-size regime where only a limited number of signals are exchanged between Alice and Bob. We compute tight numerical lower bounds in terms of the sandwiched Rényi entropy of order alpha, optimized via a two-step Frank-Wolfe algorithm, in the presence of a trusted flipping probability q. We find that trusted noise improves the key rate only for a finite interval of alpha, from the alpha -> 1 limit up to alpha approx 1.4. By optimizing on the value of alpha, we determine finite-size key rates for different values of the QBER, observing enhancement due to trusted noise both in asymptotic and finite-size regimes. Finally, we determine the maximum tolerable QBER as a function of the block size.

AI.tldr: Preprocessing noise can enhance quantum key distribution (QKD) by allowing for higher qubit error rates. This study analyzes preprocessing noise in a finite-size regime, identifying optimal conditions for key rate improvements and the maximum tolerable qubit error rate.
AI.motivation: To explore how preprocessing noise affects quantum key distribution, particularly in scenarios with limited signal exchanges, enhancing key generation capabilities even under higher error rates.
AI.method: We employ a two-step Frank-Wolfe algorithm to compute numerical lower bounds concerning the sandwiched Rényi entropy of order alpha, factoring in a trusted noise parameter q.
AI.result: Trusted noise effectively improves key rates within a specific range of alpha (1 to approximately 1.4), allowing enhanced performance in both asymptotic and finite-size contexts and revealing a correlation between block size and maximum tolerable QBER.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates that preprocessing noise can facilitate secret key generation beyond conventional limits, with potential dependencies on block size and QBER.

title: Hadron production through Higgs decay at next-to-leading order in the general-mass variable-flavor-number scheme
comment: The present work includes 9 pages with 5 figures. It is accepted to publish in Physical Review D
summary: It is known that about $60\%$ of all Higgses produced at the CERN-LHC decay into a pair of bottom quarks. Bottoms quickly hadronize, in most cases, into bottom-flavored (B) hadrons before they decay. Therefore, the study of scaled-energy distribution of B-mesons in the decay process $H\to B+Jets$ can be considered as a channel to search for the Higgs characteristics. In all previous studies, authors have ignored the mass effect of b-quarks as well as B-mesons by working in the massless scheme. In this work we, for the first time, study the mass effect of b-quarks as well as produced mesons on the scaled-energy ($x_B$) distribution of B-mesons by working in the massive scheme or general-mass variable-flavor-number scheme (GM-VFNs). We find that the meson mass is responsible for a significant enhancement of partial decay width in the low-$x_B$ region while the b-quark mass leads to an enhancement of the partial decay rate in the peak region and above.

AI.tldr: This study examines the impact of b-quark and B-meson masses on the scaled-energy distribution of B-mesons produced in Higgs decays, revealing significant enhancements in decay rates in specific energy regions.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses previous omissions in the analysis of Higgs decay to B-mesons by incorporating mass effects, aiming to refine our understanding of Higgs characteristics through B-hadron studies.
AI.method: The authors use a general-mass variable-flavor-number scheme (GM-VFNs) to account for the mass of b-quarks and B-mesons in analyzing the scaled-energy ($x_B$) distribution of B-mesons.
AI.result: The study finds that the B-meson mass significantly enhances the partial decay width in the low-$x_B$ region, while the b-quark mass increases the decay rate in the peak region and above.
